Old 5.2.2 matches new 5.2.2 (p.8) word for word, and word_changes is empty. The Annex 3 Appendix 2 2.3.4 variant is only a checklist item pointing back to 5.2.2. Page and paragraph position changed, but the documentation obligation is the same.

The first sentence of new 5.3.5.1 (p.9) is identical to the old one: the system shall aim to detect applicable system boundaries when DCAS or a feature is in 'on' mode. Only the later sentences changed, and those belong to other IDs.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system or the applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode, with the exception of the driver unavailability response.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The old text required a transition into 'stand-by' mode. The new 5.3.5.1 requires the system or applicable feature to leave 'active' mode, with an exception for the driver unavailability response. That changes both the target mode and the scope, and adds an exception.

The immediate driver notification when a boundary is exceeded is unchanged in new 5.3.5.1 (p.9). It still follows the manufacturer's strategies in 5.3.5.2 and the HMI requirements in 5.5.4.1. Only the mode-transition wording before it changed, which is covered by R-013.

The sentence 'The system shall terminate assistance to the driver provided by the affected feature or the system in a controllable way' is identical in new 5.3.5.1 (p.9). New paragraphs were added around it, but they are separate obligations and do not alter this one.
The sentence on the assistance termination strategy, to be described by the manufacturer and assessed according to Annex 3, is identical in new 5.3.5.1 (p.9). word_changes is empty.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and the driver (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre. Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The new text no longer requires that the driver is 'not detected to be disengaged'. It now requires that the driver is not deemed disengaged, as specified in 5.5.4.2.4 and 5.5.4.2.5, for more than 2 seconds immediately before the start. This adds a 2-second time qualifier and a changed criterion. The conditions (a)-(c) and the HORs exception are unchanged.
Source wording, numbered parents and resolved dependencies are unchanged; no changed definition was found for terms used here.

New 5.3.7.2.3.1 (p.12) no longer contains the statement that the requirements in 5.5.4.1.8 and subparagraphs apply. 5.5.4.1.9.1 is a different clause that applies 5.5.4.1.8 in another context. No clause in the new version carries this obligation for driver-confirmed manoeuvres, so the requirement is removed.

New 5.3.7.2.3.1 (p.12) keeps the obligation that the system be designed to give the driver sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre, as appropriate. The only difference is the dropped 'In addition,' lead-in, which followed the removed reference sentence and has no engineering effect.

Old 5.3.7.2.4.2 prohibited initiating a manoeuvre if an EOR had been presented in the preceding 7 seconds. New 5.3.7.2.4.2 (p.12) is a different obligation, requiring documented strategies for driver engagement before the manoeuvre. No candidate new clause retains the 7-second EOR initiation lockout.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The old clause required 'further' strategies 'in addition' to those in preceding clauses. The new clause 5.3.7.2.4.2 drops 'In addition, further' and refers to 'The strategies', so the obligation is no longer framed as additional strategies. The core obligation to ensure driver engagement before the manoeuvre remains.

Documentation and explanation of the driver-engagement strategies is retained in new 5.3.7.2.4.2 (page 12). The only wording difference is 'In addition, further strategies' becoming 'The strategies', which does not alter the documentation obligation. The paragraph was renumbered.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop).
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The obligation is retained in new 5.3.7.2.1.13. The word 'also' is deleted, which is not substantive. The examples changed from 'initiation of a risk mitigation function, full execution, stop the vehicle' to 'aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop', so the text is updated to reflect them.
New 5.3.7.2.4.3 (page 13) has identical wording, with no word changes. Only the paragraph number changed.
New 5.3.7.2.4.3 (page 13) contains the identical sentence on documenting the traffic situations where the system may initiate manoeuvres. Only the paragraph number changed.
New 5.3.7.2.4.4 (page 13) is identical. It still references 5.3.7.2.3.5, whose conditions (a)-(f) are unchanged in the new version. Only the paragraph number changed.
New 5.3.7.2.4.5 (page 13) is identical, with no word changes. Only the paragraph number changed. The 'propose' clause 5.3.7.2.3.6 is a separate obligation.
New 5.3.7.2.4.6 (page 13) is identical, with no word changes. Only the paragraph number changed. The reference to paragraph 6 is unchanged.
New 5.3.7.2.4.7 (page 13) is identical, with no word changes. Only the paragraph number changed. The 'propose' clause 5.3.7.2.3.8 is a separate obligation.
New 5.3.7.2.4.8 (page 13) is identical, with no word changes. Only the paragraph number changed.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The system shall only initiate a manoeuvre if the vehicle is located on a highway or a highway-like road and it is not withholding HORs.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The old clause 5.3.7.2.4.10 has no counterpart in the shown new text. Its gate on initiating manoeuvres (highway including slip roads, and not withholding HORs) was not found as a manoeuvre-initiation restriction in the candidates. The new 5.5.4.2.6.5 only permits withholding HORs on 'Highway' or 'Highway-like' roads up to 130 km/h. That broader scope and the new speed limit are not a restatement of the old obligation. Neither the old paragraph nor new 5.3.7.2.4.x clauses show the old gate, so I cannot confirm it persists. The related 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 change shows highway-like roads are now in scope. Because the new text does not state the old gate, I cannot restate it. Removal is more supportable than modification.

Old 5.3.7.2.4.11 sentence is carried in new 5.3.7.2.4.9 (page 13) in identical wording: the acknowledgement request is given while the vehicle is stopped. Only the paragraph number changed. Reference 5.6 content is also unchanged.

New 5.3.7.2.4.9 keeps the at-least-monthly request and the extension for user differentiation. The only difference is 'three months' becoming '3 months', a formatting change with no change in the obligation.
New 5.3.7.2.4.9 keeps the sentence that the request need not be repeated for a driver the vehicle can identify as having already acknowledged it. Only the paragraph number changed.
New 5.3.7.2.4.9 keeps the sentence that the request shall be given in the current drive cycle if the current driver has not acknowledged before. Only the paragraph number changed.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or continuing operation if capable).
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: New 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 adds 'or highway-like road' to the operating scope. This widens the condition under which the obligation applies; the rest of the wording is unchanged.
The lane-marking recognition sentence is word-for-word identical in new 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 (page 14), including the R130 reference. It was only renumbered from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The system's driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk Mitigation Function (RMF).
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: New 5.3.7.3.1 changes the subject of the obligation from 'the system' to 'the system's driver unavailability response', narrowing what must comply with R79 RMF requirements. The reference and series of amendments are unchanged.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.

The obligation changes from activating the RMF to stopping in accordance with its requirements; the trigger condition is unchanged.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a relevant intended manoeuvre or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and amount of other road users present.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: New 5.5.4.1.9.2 specifies the information as visual and adds an 'at least 3 seconds ahead' timing alternative to the sufficient-notice criterion. This changes the obligation's scope and quantitative target.

The sentence on reduced time and informing visually as far in advance as possible in the event of imminent collision or conflict with ongoing-manoeuvre information is word-for-word identical in new 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.20). Only the preceding sentence and the following evidence sentence changed, and they are separate obligations.

The sentence requiring lane change initiation to be announced by another modality unless the driver has observed the visual information is absent from new 5.5.4.1.9.2 (p.20). The clause now ends with the 3-second evidence provision, and no other candidate clause contains the lane-change announcement requirement.
New 5.5.4.2.2.1 (p.20) is identical to the old text; only the page changed.
The text is identical in the new version, now numbered 5.5.4.2.2.2 (p.20) instead of 5.5.4.2.2.3. This is renumbering only.
New 5.5.4.2.3.2.1 (p.21) is identical to the old text; only the page changed.

The first sentence of 5.5.4.2.5.2 on visual disengagement is identical in the new version (p.21). The dashboard and instrument panel exception was changed in a separate sentence, but the disengagement definition itself is unchanged.

The sentence requiring the manufacturer to specify an outline of the driving task relevant areas and when they are relevant is identical in new 5.5.4.2.5.2 (p.21). The dashboard and instrument panel sentence was revised separately and does not alter this documentation obligation.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: For the purpose of the assessment of visual disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered as a driving task relevant area only while manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed for a maximum duration of 3 seconds.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: Old text said the dashboard and instrument panel shall not be considered a driving task relevant area. New 5.5.4.2.5.2 reverses this: they may be considered relevant only while manoeuvre relevant information is displayed, for at most 3 seconds.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture if either is re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for a sufficient duration depending on the situation.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: New 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 deletes 'engaged or' so only reengagement following an aversion is covered. It also adds an exception: re-direction towards the dashboard and instrument panel does not count. The comma is only formatting.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The duration for which the driver's eye gaze or head posture must be re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for the driver to be deemed visually reengaged shall be at least 200 milliseconds.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The 200 ms minimum is unchanged. The target it applies to now excludes the dashboard and instrument panel, and the clause covers reengagement only, not 'engaged or'.
New 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 has identical wording (no word changes): EOR escalated at the latest 3 seconds after the initial EOR with increased intensity. Only the page and the surrounding clauses differ.
New 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 keeps the sentence 'The escalated EOR shall always contain acoustic and/or haptic information' word for word.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for section 9, the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld when the vehicle is located on a “Highway” or a “Highway-like” road and is operated at a speed up to 130 km/h, as outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The documentation duty is unchanged. The scope of the withholding condition is widened: new 5.5.4.2.6.5 covers “Highway” or “Highway-like” roads, where the old text covered only “Highway”.
New 5.5.4.2.6.5.3 is identical: if the system can suppress accelerator input to avoid exceeding system boundaries, the driver shall be able to override this. No word changes.

New 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 is identical, including the table (3.5 s at 130 km/h, 5.0 s at 10 to 60 km/h) and the 'Notwithstanding 5.5.4.2.6.2.1' reference. The referenced clause 5.5.4.2.6.2.1 is also unchanged.
The new 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 sentence on linear interpolation between 60 and 130 km/h is identical to the old one. No word changes.

New 5.5.4.2.7.1 has the same obligation: the driver state monitoring system has strategies to assess driver disengagement when no driver input is determined over prolonged periods, and implements countermeasures. 'Be equipped with' became 'have', which is wording only. The added example 'or assessment of changes in gaze direction' is a non-limiting e.g. and does not change the obligation.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The driver state monitoring system shall have strategies to assess whether the driver is disengaged in the event that no driver input has been determined over prolonged periods (e.g. through a negative determination of driver drowsiness or assessment of changes in gaze direction), and implement appropriate countermeasures.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: Clause relocated to 5.5.4.2.7.1. 'Be equipped with' became 'have', which is not substantive. The example list of ways to determine no driver input now also includes 'assessment of changes in gaze direction', which broadens the illustrative scope, so the text is updated.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The system shall be disabled for a period of at least 30 minutes whilst the powertrain is active when the driver is detected to have insufficient engagement. The disablement shall happen once the driver has resumed control of the vehicle, or the vehicle has become stationary.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The core 30-minute disablement wording is unchanged. A new sentence adds a timing condition: the disablement happens once the driver has resumed control or the vehicle has become stationary. This changes when the disablement takes effect, so the requirement is modified.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: When the system is disabled due to insufficient engagement by the driver, the system shall only be re-enabled after the driver has confirmed by a deliberate action their understanding of their responsibilities and appropriate use of the system.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The old obligation was to request that the driver read the driver information material (paragraph 5.6) by the latest upon powertrain deactivation. The new 5.5.4.2.8.4 replaces it with a re-enablement condition requiring deliberate driver confirmation of understanding. The obligation, trigger and target have changed.

coverage.source_unit: 2.1 Definition of DCAS as hardware and software capable of assisting driver in longitudinal and lateral control on a sustained basis; also referred to as 'the system'

obligations.text: 'Driver Control Assistance System (DCAS)' means the hardware and software collectively capable of assisting a driver in controlling the longitudinal and lateral motion of the vehicle on a sustained basis; within this UN Regulation DCAS is also referred to as 'the system'.
obligations.reason: Identical definition to old 2.1 (o020); same term and scope, no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 2.2 definition lead-in with (a) and (b): vehicles not differing in DCAS system characteristics/design and vehicle features significantly influencing DCAS performance

obligations.text: A vehicle type with regard to DCAS is a group of vehicles that do not differ in essential aspects: (a) the system characteristics and design of DCAS; (b) vehicle features which significantly influence the performance of DCAS.
obligations.reason: Same definition and scope as old clause o021 (2.2), identical wording and page; continuity as the same type-grouping criterion.

obligations.text: If, within the manufacturer's designation of the vehicle type, DCAS consists of multiple features some of which may optionally not be fitted on some vehicles, a DCAS with lesser features is deemed to belong to the same vehicle type with respect to DCAS.
obligations.reason: Identical to the final sentence of old clause o021 (2.2); same scope of optional feature grouping within one vehicle type.

coverage.source_unit: 2.3 definition of (DCAS) Feature

obligations.text: A (DCAS) Feature is a specific DCAS capability providing assistance to the driver in defined traffic scenarios, circumstances and system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same definition as old clause o022 (2.3), identical wording, same paragraph and page.

coverage.source_unit: 2.4 definition of Dynamic Control (real-time operational and tactical functions, including lateral/longitudinal control, monitoring, responding, planning)

obligations.text: Dynamic Control means the real-time performance of operational and tactical functions required to move the vehicle, including controlling lateral and longitudinal motion, monitoring the road environment, responding to events in road traffic, and planning and signalling for manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o023 (2.4), same paragraph and page.

obligations.text: For the purpose of this Regulation, DCAS assists the driver by carrying out operational and tactical functions without limiting the driver's ability to intervene at any given time.
obligations.reason: Identical to last sentence of old clause o023 (2.4); same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 2.5 definition of System Boundaries

obligations.text: System Boundaries are the verifiable or measurable limits or conditions established by a manufacturer up to or within which DCAS or a DCAS feature is designed to provide assistance to the driver, and those conditions which impact the system's ability to operate as intended.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o024 (2.5), same paragraph and page.

coverage.source_unit: 2.6 definition of Driver disengagement

obligations.text: Driver disengagement means the system's determination of the driver's current inability to safely execute perception, planning, or decision-making and to intervene in the operation of DCAS.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o025 (2.6), same paragraph and page.

coverage.source_unit: 2.7 definition of Operational functions (basic driver control actions incl. lateral/longitudinal motion)
2.7 last sentence: realization implies driver's physical operation of vehicle

obligations.text: Operational functions means the basic control actions of the driver required and taken to move a vehicle and operate its systems, including control of the vehicle's lateral and longitudinal motion.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o026 (2.7), same paragraph and page.

obligations.text: Realization of operational functions implies the driver's physical operation of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Identical to last sentence of old clause o026 (2.7); same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 2.8 definition of “Tactical functions” (whole clause)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Pure definition; does not impose an engineering, test or compliance obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 2.9 definition of “Real-time” (whole clause)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Pure definition; does not impose an engineering, test or compliance obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 2.10 definition of “Manoeuvre”, including series-of-manoeuvres rule (whole clause)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Pure definition; no mandatory action or requirement imposed.

coverage.source_unit: 2.11 definition of “Target Lane” (whole clause)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Pure definition; no mandatory action or requirement imposed.

coverage.source_unit: 2.12 definition of “Lane Change Procedure (LCP)” with list items (a)-(e)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition describing a sequence of operations; imposes no standalone requirement.

coverage.source_unit: 2.13 definition of “Lane Change Manoeuvre (LCM)” with (a) start and (b) end criteria
coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition of start and end points; imposes no standalone requirement.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; it sets no engineering, test or compliance requirement of its own.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; it sets no engineering, test or compliance requirement of its own.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; it sets no engineering, test or compliance requirement of its own.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; does not impose an engineering, test or compliance obligation by itself.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; no mandatory action or requirement is imposed.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; no mandatory action or requirement is imposed.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; no mandatory action or requirement is imposed.

coverage.source_unit: 2.20 definition of 'Current maximum speed'
coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; no mandatory action or requirement is imposed.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; the obligation to provide the R171SWIN is in separate clauses (e.g. 10.3).

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; does not impose an engineering, test or compliance requirement.

coverage.source_unit: 2.29 definition of 'Automated Driving System (ADS)'
2.30 definition of 'Dynamic Driving Task (DDT)'

coverage.source_unit: Heading '3. Application for approval'
3.1 application for approval shall be submitted by manufacturer or authorized representative to the Type Approval Authority per Schedule 3 of the 1958 Agreement

obligations.text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to the DCAS shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by the manufacturer's authorized representative to the Type Approval Authority of the Contracting Party, according to the provisions of Schedule 3 of the 1958 Agreement.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o057 (3.1): same actor, action, recipient and Schedule 3 scope; only relocated to a new page with no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 3.2 application shall be accompanied by the following documentation (introductory sentence for list 3.2.x)

obligations.text: The application for approval shall be accompanied by the documentation specified in the following sub-paragraphs of paragraph 3.2.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o058 (3.2): identical introductory requirement that the application be accompanied by documentation, same scope and parent paragraph 3; no change.

coverage.source_unit: 3.2.1 description of vehicle type per paragraph 2.2 with documentation package per Annex 1 giving access to basic design of DCAS and its links to other vehicle systems or direct control of output variables

obligations.text: The application shall be accompanied by a description of the vehicle type with regard to the items specified in paragraph 2.2, together with a documentation package as required in Annex 1 which gives access to the basic design of the DCAS and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems, or by which it directly controls output variables.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o059 (3.2.1): same documentation item under 3.2 with same Annex 1 and para 2.2 references; only a punctuation difference.

coverage.source_unit: 3.3 representative vehicle of the type to be approved shall be submitted to the Type Approval Authority or designated technical service
Heading '4. Approval'

obligations.text: A vehicle representative of the vehicle type to be approved shall be submitted to the Type Approval Authority or its designated technical service responsible for conducting the approval tests.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o060 (3.3): same actor, object and recipient; unchanged text relocated to a new page.

coverage.source_unit: 4.1 if the vehicle type meets requirements of paragraphs 5 to 10, approval shall be granted

obligations.text: If the vehicle type submitted for approval pursuant to this UN Regulation meets the requirements of paragraphs 5 to 10, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o061 (4.1): same condition (paragraphs 5 to 10) and same approval-granting obligation; no change.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2 sentence 1-2: approval number assigned to each type approved; first two digits indicate amendment series
4.2 sentence 3: same Contracting Party shall not assign same number to another vehicle type

obligations.text: An approval number shall be assigned to each type approved; its first two digits (at present 00 for the Regulation in its original form) shall indicate the series of amendments incorporating the technical amendments made at the time of issue of the approval.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o062 (4.2), identical wording and context, renumbered page only.

obligations.text: The same Contracting Party shall not assign the same approval number to another type of vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o062 (4.2) final sentence, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 4.3 whole paragraph: communication of approval/extension/refusal/withdrawal/production discontinued by Annex 1 form with documentation max A4 or electronic

obligations.text: Communication of approval, extension, refusal, withdrawal of approval or definitive discontinuation of production of a vehicle type shall be sent to the Contracting Parties by a form conforming to the model in Annex 1 and documentation supplied by the applicant in a format not exceeding A4 (210 × 297 mm), on an appropriate scale or in electronic format.
obligations.reason: Identical to o063 (4.3) in actor, action and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 4.4 intro: affix approval mark conspicuously in readily accessible place specified on approval form to every conforming vehicle

obligations.text: There shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under this Regulation, an international approval mark conforming to the model in Annex 2.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as o064 (4.4), identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.4.1 (a)-(b): mark composition: circle around E, country number, regulation number R, dash, approval number

obligations.text: The approval mark shall consist of a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by (a) the distinguishing number of the country which granted approval and (b) the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle.
obligations.reason: Same as o065 (4.4.1) under the same parent 4.4; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 4.5 whole: approval mark clearly legible and indelible

obligations.text: The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
obligations.reason: Identical to o066 (4.5).

coverage.source_unit: 4.6: Type Approval Authority shall verify CoP arrangements before granting approval
5. General Specifications: manufacturer shall demonstrate fulfilment of provisions to TAA during safety approach inspection per Annex 3 and Annex 4 tests

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall verify the existence of satisfactory arrangements for ensuring effective checks on conformity of production before type-approval is granted.
obligations.reason: Same as o067 (4.6), unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall demonstrate fulfilment of the provisions of paragraph 5 (General Specifications) to the Type Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety approach as part of the assessment to Annex 3 and according to the relevant tests in Annex 4.
obligations.reason: Same as the paragraph 5 intro text included in o067; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1. General Requirements (heading)
5.1.1 system designed to ensure driver remains engaged per 5.5.4.2

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to ensure the driver remains engaged with the driving task, in accordance with paragraph 5.5.4.2.
obligations.reason: Renumbered/relocated page only; identical scoped design obligation to old 5.1.1 (o069) under same parent 5.1 General Requirements; actor, action and reference to 5.5.4.2 unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.2 design for mode awareness and avoid overreliance, demonstrated by fulfilment of 5.5.4

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to ensure mode awareness and avoid driver overreliance, demonstrated by fulfilment of the provisions of paragraphs 5.5.4.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old 5.1.2 (o070), same parent 5.1; wording and demonstration reference to 5.5.4 unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.3 guard against foreseeable misuse and unauthorized modification of software and hardware

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to guard against reasonably foreseeable misuse by the driver and unauthorized modification of the system's software and hardware components.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old 5.1.3 (o071), same parent 5.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.4 means to safely override or deactivate at any time per 5.5.3.4

obligations.text: The system shall provide the driver a means to safely override or deactivate the system at any time in accordance with paragraphs 5.5.3.4.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old 5.1.4 (o072), same parent 5.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.5 sentence 1: DCAS vehicle at least equipped with AEBS
5.1.5 sentence 2: additionally equipped with LDPS or LDWS
5.1.5 sentence 3: systems comply with UN Regulations 131, 152, 79 (CSF) and 130 as appropriate for vehicle category

obligations.text: The DCAS-equipped vehicle shall at least be equipped with an Advanced Emergency Braking System.
obligations.reason: Same scoped fitment obligation as old 5.1.5 (o073), same parent 5.1; unchanged.

obligations.text: In addition to the Advanced Emergency Braking System, the DCAS-equipped vehicle shall be equipped with either a Lane Departure Prevention System or a Lane Departure Warning System.
obligations.reason: Same scoped fitment obligation as old 5.1.5 (o073); unchanged.

obligations.text: The required AEBS and lane departure systems shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of UN Regulations Nos. 131, 152, 79 (Corrective Steering Function) and 130, as appropriate for the DCAS-equipped vehicle category.
obligations.reason: Same compliance obligation as old 5.1.5 (o073); unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2 heading: DCAS interaction with other vehicle assistance systems and ADS
5.2.1 first sentence: in 'active' mode, system operation shall not deactivate or suppress longitudinal functionality of activated emergency assistance systems (AEBS)
5.2.1 second sentence: for lateral functionality, system may deactivate or suppress emergency assistance systems per respective regulations

obligations.text: While the DCAS is in 'active' mode, its operation shall not deactivate or suppress the longitudinal functionality of activated emergency assistance systems (i.e., AEBS).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o075 (5.2.1), identical wording, same paragraph number, relocated to page 8 only.

obligations.text: In the case of lateral functionality, the DCAS in 'active' mode may deactivate or suppress emergency assistance systems, in accordance with the respective regulations covering this functionality.
obligations.reason: Same permission as the second sentence of old o075 (5.2.1); unchanged scope and condition.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.2: manufacturer documentation of transitions between DCAS and other assistance/automation systems, prioritization, and suppression/deactivation of other safety assistance systems

obligations.text: Transitions between DCAS and other assistance or automation systems, prioritization of one over the other, and any suppression or deactivation of other assistance systems intended to ensure safe and nominal operation of the vehicle shall be described in detail in the documentation presented to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o076 (5.2.2); same actor, object and documentation scope. Annex 3 item o567 is a separate documentation item.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3 first part: DCAS shall be switched to 'OFF' mode upon activation of an ADS feature
5.2.3 second part: DCAS shall not be able to be switched to 'ON' while an ADS feature is active

obligations.text: DCAS shall be switched to 'OFF' mode upon activation of an ADS feature.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; no candidate (o195, o196, o203) addresses ADS activation forcing DCAS off. Interaction with ADS is a new scope.

obligations.text: DCAS shall not be able to be switched to 'ON' mode whilst an ADS feature is active.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; o203 only requires deliberate driver action for off-to-on, not blocking activation during ADS operation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3 heading: Functional requirements
5.3.1: manufacturer shall describe in detail in the documentation the detection capabilities relevant to individual features, especially system boundaries listed in Annex 3 Appendix 3

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe in detail in the documentation the detection capabilities of the system relevant to the individual features, especially for those system boundaries listed in Annex 3, Appendix 3.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o078 (5.3.1); same actor, action and documentation scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.2 – system shall detect, assess and respond to surroundings within system boundaries and to the extent possible beyond them

obligations.text: The system shall be able to detect, assess and respond to its surroundings as required to implement the system's intended functionality, within the system boundaries and to the extent possible if operating beyond system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o079 (5.3.2), same paragraph number, identical actor, action and scope; only page layout differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.2.1 – system shall aim to avoid disruption to traffic flow by adapting behaviour

obligations.text: The system shall aim to avoid disruption to the flow of traffic by adapting its behaviour to the surrounding traffic in an appropriate safety-oriented way.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o080 (5.3.2.1) under the same parent 5.3.2; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.2.2 – if risk of collision detected, aim to avoid or mitigate severity

obligations.text: If the system detects a risk of collision, it shall aim to avoid or mitigate the severity of a collision.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o081 (5.3.2.2) with same parent and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.2.3 – control longitudinal and lateral motion aiming to maintain appropriate distances from other road users

obligations.text: Without prejudice to other requirements in this UN Regulation, the system shall control the longitudinal and lateral motion of the vehicle aiming to maintain appropriate distances from other road users.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o082 (5.3.2.3) with same parent and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.3 – permission for system to activate relevant vehicle systems when necessary and applicable

obligations.text: The system may activate relevant vehicle systems when necessary and applicable as appropriate for the system's operational design (e.g. direction indicators, activate wipers in case of rain, heating systems, etc.).
obligations.reason: Identical permission to old clause o083 (5.3.3), same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.4 – control strategy designed to reduce collision risk while remaining controllable, accounting for driver reaction time per 5.3.6

obligations.text: The system's control strategy shall be designed to reduce the risk of collisions whilst remaining controllable, accounting for the reaction time of the driver, as per paragraph 5.3.6.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o084 (5.3.4) with same scope; only the page number differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5. heading 'Response to System boundaries'
5.3.5.1 para 1 sentence 1: system shall aim to detect applicable system boundaries when DCAS/feature in 'on' mode
5.3.5.1 para 1 sentence 2: on boundary exceeded, system/feature leaves 'active' mode (except driver unavailability response) and immediately notifies driver
5.3.5.1 para 2: driver disengaged while boundary exceeded - continue assistance or terminate gradually
5.3.5.1 para 3 sentence 1: driver state monitoring continues until driver motorically and visually reengaged
5.3.5.1 para 3 sentence 2: initiate driver unavailability response within 10 s if driver remains disengaged
5.3.5.1 para 4 sentence 1: terminate assistance in controllable way
5.3.5.1 para 4 sentence 2: manufacturer describes termination strategy, assessed per Annex 3

obligations.text: When DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode, the system shall aim to detect the applicable system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same detection obligation as old 5.3.5.1 sentence 1, unchanged wording and scope.

obligations.text: If the system identifies that the system or feature boundary is exceeded, the system or applicable feature shall leave the 'active' mode (with the exception of the driver unavailability response) and immediately notify the driver per the manufacturer-described strategies of 5.3.5.2 and the HMI requirements of 5.5.4.1.
obligations.reason: Replaces old requirement to transition into 'stand-by' mode with leaving 'active' mode, adding exception for driver unavailability response; notification unchanged.

obligations.text: If the driver is detected to be disengaged while the system or feature boundary is detected to be exceeded, the system shall continue providing lateral and longitudinal assistance to the extent possible or terminate assistance gradually in a controllable way, as outlined in the manufacturer's safety concept.
obligations.reason: No equivalent in old 5.3.5.1; new disengaged-driver case.

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system shall continue to monitor driver disengagement until the driver is motorically and visually reengaged.
obligations.reason: New monitoring requirement not in old clause.

obligations.text: The system shall initiate a driver unavailability response at the latest 10 seconds after it has detected being beyond a system boundary, if the driver remains disengaged.
obligations.reason: New 10 s timing requirement not in old clause.

obligations.text: The system shall terminate assistance provided by the affected feature or the system in a controllable way.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.3.5.1 final paragraph sentence 1.

obligations.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall describe the assistance termination strategy, which shall be assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.3.5.1 final paragraph sentence 2.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.1.1 whole sentence

obligations.text: The system shall aim to avoid rapid system fluctuations between 'stand-by' and 'active' modes.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.3.5.1.1 under same parent.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.2 whole sentence: manufacturer documentation of boundary conditions and notification strategies

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for Section 9, the system boundary conditions for the system and its features, and the strategies to notify the driver when a boundary condition is detected to be exceeded, being met or being approached (per paragraph 5.3.5.5).
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.3.5.2.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.2.1 whole sentence

obligations.text: The manufacturer's boundary condition description shall at least take into account potentially relevant boundary conditions listed in Annex 3, Appendix 3.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.3.5.2.1.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.2.2 whole sentence

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe and, where reasonable, demonstrate the behaviour of the system, the impact on system performance and how safety is ensured if the system or its features remain in 'active' mode beyond the system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.3.5.2.2.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.3 first limb: manufacturer shall identify system boundaries the system is able to detect
5.3.5.3 second limb: manufacturer shall describe means of identifying system boundaries

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall identify those system boundaries that the system is able to detect.
obligations.reason: Same scoped manufacturer identification obligation as o091 (5.3.5.3), same paragraph number, identical wording and parent 5.3.5 Response to System boundaries; only page shifted (8 to 9).

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe the means by which the system is capable of identifying system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same scoped description obligation as o091 (5.3.5.3), unchanged wording and context; only page differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.4 first limb: any declared system boundary the system is unable to detect shall be documented
5.3.5.4 second limb: justification to Type Approval Authority satisfaction that inability to detect does not affect safe operation

obligations.text: Any declared system boundary that the system is unable to detect shall be documented.
obligations.reason: Matches o092 (5.3.5.4), identical wording and parent 5.3.5; same scoped documentation obligation, only page renumbered.

obligations.text: For any declared system boundary that the system is unable to detect, it shall be justified, to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority, how the inability to detect does not affect the safe operation of the system or its features.
obligations.reason: Matches o092 (5.3.5.4), identical justification obligation and context; only page differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.5.5 whole paragraph: when approaching a system boundary of a feature in active mode, inform driver with sufficient lead time

obligations.text: When the system identifies that the vehicle is approaching a system boundary of a feature in 'active mode', it shall inform the driver of this with sufficient lead time for the driver to respond appropriately.
obligations.reason: Identical to o093 (5.3.5.5) with same parent 5.3.5 and scope; only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6 heading 'Controllability'
5.3.6.1 first sentence: system designed so control actions (incl. failures, boundaries, cancelling manoeuvres, switch to off) remain controllable
5.3.6.1 second sentence: design shall take into account driver's potential reaction time incl. manual reengagement so intervention can be safely performed at any time

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to ensure that control actions by the system, including but not limited to those resulting from system failures, reaching system boundaries, cancelling manoeuvres or when the system is being switched to 'off' mode, remain controllable for the driver.
obligations.reason: Identical to o095 (5.3.6.1) under same parent 5.3.6 Controllability; only page changed.

obligations.text: The controllability design shall take into account the driver's potential reaction time, as relevant to the situation, including manual reengagement where applicable, so that driver intervention can be safely performed at any time (e.g., during a given manoeuvre).
obligations.reason: Same second sentence of o095 (5.3.6.1), unchanged scope and wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6.1.1 first sentence: whilst withholding HORs, manufacturer shall consider driver reaction time to respond to DCA and hold steering
5.3.6.1.1 second sentence: reaction time never assumed less than 1 second unless controllability demonstrated through specific strategies

obligations.text: Whilst withholding HORs, the manufacturer shall consider the potential reaction time required for the driver to respond to a DCA and to hold the steering control.
obligations.reason: Identical to o096 (5.3.6.1.1) under same parent 5.3.6.1; only page numbering differs.

obligations.text: When considering the driver reaction time whilst withholding HORs, it shall never be assumed to be less than 1 second, unless the manufacturer is able to demonstrate that controllability is ensured through specific strategies.
obligations.reason: Same 1 second limit and exception as o096 (5.3.6.1.1), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6.1.2 sentence 1: manufacturer shall consider time for driver to direct gaze to driving-task-relevant areas after a DCA given during a system-initiated manoeuvre
5.3.6.1.2 sentence 2: if DCA given whilst withholding HORs, this time considered in addition to 5.3.6.1.1 time
5.3.6.1.2 sentence 3: manufacturer shall explain strategies and timing of assistance until DCA confirmed

obligations.text: If a DCA is given while performing a system-initiated manoeuvre, the manufacturer shall consider the time required for the driver to direct their gaze to appropriate driving task relevant area(s) after the DCA is given in order to control the vehicle in the current situation when responding to this DCA.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; old 5.3.6.1.1 covers only reaction time to respond to a DCA and hold the steering control while withholding HORs (min 1 s), not gaze-direction time in system-initiated manoeuvres. No evidence of same scoped obligation.

obligations.text: If the DCA is given whilst withholding HORs during a system-initiated manoeuvre, the manufacturer shall consider the time for the driver to direct their gaze to driving task relevant area(s) in addition to the time required by paragraph 5.3.6.1.1.
obligations.reason: Additive-time requirement is new; it builds on o096 but is a separate scoped obligation for DCA during system-initiated manoeuvres.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the strategies and the timing with which the assistance is to be provided to the driver until the DCA is confirmed.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause requires explaining assistance strategies and timing until DCA confirmation; o086 concerns termination strategy at system boundaries.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6.2 sentence 1: system designed to ensure controllability per capabilities and within boundaries
5.3.6.2 sentence 2: when HORs withheld, system shall take into account driver may be motorically disengaged
5.3.6.2 sentence 3: manufacturer shall describe controllability design in detail to TAA, assessed per Annex 3

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to ensure controllability in accordance with the system's capabilities and within the defined system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Identical text and scope to old o097 (same paragraph number 5.3.6.2, same parent Controllability); no change.

obligations.text: In the case that HORs are being withheld, the system shall take into account that the driver may be motorically disengaged.
obligations.reason: Identical to the corresponding sentence in o097, same paragraph and scope.

obligations.text: The manufacturer's controllability design shall be described in detail to the Type Approval Authority and shall be assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Identical to the corresponding sentence in o097, same paragraph and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6.3 heading 'Deceleration and Acceleration'
5.3.6.3.1 main requirement: system-controlled deceleration and acceleration manageable for driver and surrounding traffic, unless increased deceleration required for safety

obligations.text: When controlled by the system, the vehicle deceleration and acceleration shall remain manageable for the driver and surrounding traffic, unless increased levels of deceleration are required to ensure the safety of the vehicle or surrounding road users.
obligations.reason: Identical text, same paragraph number and parent 5.3.6.3 as old o099; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.6.3.2: while maintaining constant speed without external disturbances, aim to minimise unreasonable speed fluctuations

obligations.text: While the system is trying to maintain a constant speed without external disturbances, it shall aim to minimise unreasonable fluctuations in the vehicle's speed.
obligations.reason: Identical text, same paragraph and parent as old o100; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7 heading 'System Dynamic Control'
5.3.7.1 heading: Positioning of the vehicle in the lane of travel
5.3.7.1.1 first sentence: system in 'active' mode shall assist in keeping vehicle stable within lane
5.3.7.1.1 second sentence: in 'active' mode system shall ensure vehicle does not leave lane for manufacturer-specified lateral accelerations

obligations.text: While in 'active' mode, the system shall assist in keeping the vehicle in a stable position within its lane of travel.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o103 (same paragraph number 5.3.7.1.1, identical wording, same parent 5.3.7.1); only page changed from 9 to 10.

obligations.text: While in 'active' mode, the system shall ensure that the vehicle does not leave its lane of travel for lateral acceleration values specified by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as second sentence of o103; unchanged text and context, only pagination differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.1.1.1 system shall have capability to adapt vehicle speed in response to road curvature to achieve lane keeping

obligations.text: The system shall have the capability to adapt the vehicle speed in response to road curvature in order to keep the vehicle in a stable position within its lane of travel (per 5.3.7.1.1).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o104; identical wording, same paragraph number and parent context, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.1.2 first sentence: activated feature shall at any time within boundary conditions ensure vehicle does not unintentionally cross lane marking for manufacturer-specified lateral accelerations not exceeding 3 m/s² (M1, N1) and 2.5 m/s² (M2, M3, N2, N3)
5.3.7.1.2 recognition sentence (max values may not be achievable e.g. weather, tyres, slopes) and sentence: feature shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch control strategy
5.3.7.1.2 permission: system may exceed specified max lateral acceleration by not more than 0.3 m/s² within category caps
5.3.7.1.2 'Notwithstanding' paragraph: for periods of at most 2 s may exceed by up to 40 per cent within caps

obligations.text: The activated feature shall at any time, within the boundary conditions, ensure that the vehicle does not unintentionally cross a lane marking for lateral acceleration values specified by the manufacturer, which shall not exceed 3 m/s² for M1 and N1 category vehicles and 2.5 m/s² for M2, M3, N2 and N3 category vehicles.
obligations.reason: Same as first sentence of o105; identical wording and context.

obligations.text: Where the manufacturer-specified maximum lateral acceleration is not achievable under all conditions (e.g., inclement weather, different tyres fitted, laterally sloped roads), the feature shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy in these other conditions.
obligations.reason: Same as corresponding sentence of o105; unchanged.

obligations.text: The system may exceed the specified value of maximum lateral acceleration by not more than 0.3 m/s², while not exceeding 3 m/s² for M1 and N1 category vehicles and 2.5 m/s² for M2, M3, N2 and N3 category vehicles.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o105; unchanged.

obligations.text: For time periods of not more than 2 seconds, the lateral acceleration of the system may exceed the specified value of maximum lateral acceleration by not more than 40 per cent, while not exceeding 3 m/s² for M1 and N1 category vehicles and 2.5 m/s² for M2, M3, N2 and N3 category vehicles by more than 0.3 m/s².
obligations.reason: Same permission as the 'Notwithstanding' paragraph of o105; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.1.2.1 moving average over 0.5 s of lateral jerk shall not exceed 5 m/s³

obligations.text: The moving average over half a second of the lateral jerk generated by the system shall not exceed 5 m/s³.
obligations.reason: Same as o106; identical wording and the same parent 5.3.7.1.2 context (not the lane-change o305 scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.1.3 strategy for determining speed and lateral acceleration shall be documented and assessed by Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: The strategy by which the system determines the appropriate speed and resulting lateral acceleration shall be documented (by the manufacturer) and assessed by the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same as o107; identical wording, same paragraph number and parent context.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.1.4 first sentence: at boundary conditions (9.1.3), no steering input and front tyre unintentionally crossing lane marking, avoid sudden loss of steering support by continued assistance
5.3.7.1.4 second sentence: inform driver by optical warning plus acoustic or haptic warning
5.3.7.1.4 second paragraph: M2/M3/N2/N3 warning requirement deemed fulfilled with UN R130 LDWS

obligations.text: When the system reaches its boundary conditions set out in paragraph 9.1.3., in the absence of any driver input to the steering control and when any front tyre of the vehicle starts to unintentionally cross a lane marking, the system shall avoid sudden loss of steering support by providing continued assistance to the extent possible as outlined in the safety concept of the vehicle manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o108 (same paragraph number, same conditions and action); only wording changed from 'any the front tyre' to 'any front tyre'. Editorial correction.

obligations.text: In the same situation (boundary conditions per 9.1.3, no driver steering input, front tyre unintentionally crossing a lane marking), the system shall clearly inform the driver about this system status by means of an optical warning signal and additionally by an acoustic or haptic warning signal.
obligations.reason: Identical to the second sentence of o108 at the same paragraph; no substantive change.

obligations.text: For vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2 and N3, the warning requirement of paragraph 5.3.7.1.4 is deemed fulfilled if the vehicle is equipped with a Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS) fulfilling the technical requirements of UN Regulation No. 130.
obligations.reason: Identical permission/deeming provision in o108 at the same paragraph; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2 heading 'Manoeuvre'
5.3.7.2.1 heading 'General Requirements'
5.3.7.2.1.1 main rule: manoeuvre only initiated if driver not deemed disengaged for more than 2 s immediately prior to start, and (a)/(b)/(c) per manoeuvre type
5.3.7.2.1.1 last sentence: motoric disengagement not considered when HORs withheld by system

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall only be initiated if the driver is not deemed to be disengaged (as specified in paragraphs 5.5.4.2.4. and 5.5.4.2.5.) for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to its start, and: (a) has commanded the system to perform the manoeuvre for a driver-initiated manoeuvre; or (b) has acknowledged the system's intention as needed for a driver-confirmed manoeuvre; or (c) is given sufficient notice to react for a system-initiated manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Replaces o111 (same paragraph, same manoeuvre-initiation condition); changed from 'not detected to be disengaged' to 'not deemed disengaged for more than 2 seconds immediately prior to start' with reference to 5.5.4.2.4/5.5.4.2.5.

obligations.text: Motoric disengagement may not be considered when HORs are being withheld by the system.
obligations.reason: Same sentence as in o111 at the same paragraph; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.2 whole paragraph: manoeuvre only if detection capability with sufficient range front, side, rear

obligations.text: The system shall only be permitted to perform a manoeuvre if the vehicle is equipped with detection capabilities with sufficient range to the front, side and rear with respect to the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Identical to o112 at same paragraph number; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.3 whole paragraph: no manoeuvre initiation while driver disengagement warning is given

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall not be initiated if a driver disengagement warning is being given to the driver.
obligations.reason: Identical to o113 at same paragraph number; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.4 whole sentence: no manoeuvre initiation if collision risk detected in predicted path

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall not be initiated if a risk of collision with another vehicle or road user is detected in the predicted path of the DCAS vehicle during the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation renumbered/relocated to page 11 with identical paragraph number and wording; matches old clause o114 (same actor, action, and collision-risk condition).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.5 whole sentence: manoeuvre predictable and manageable for other road users

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall be predictable and manageable for other road users.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number and wording as old o115 within the same General Requirements context; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.6 whole sentence: manoeuvre shall aim to be one continuous movement

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall aim to be one continuous movement.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number and wording as old o116 in the same General Requirements context; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.7 whole sentence: manoeuvre completed without undue delay

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall be completed without undue delay.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number and wording as old o117 in the same General Requirements context; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.8 whole sentence: after manoeuvre completion, system resumes assisting lane position

obligations.text: Once a manoeuvre has been completed, the system shall resume assisting in maintaining a stable position in the lane of travel.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number and wording as old o118 in the same General Requirements context; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.9 mandatory: visual warning if vehicle unexpectedly forced stationary during planned manoeuvre
5.3.7.2.1.9 permission: system may request driver to resume control

obligations.text: In case the vehicle is unexpectedly forced to become stationary during a planned manoeuvre, the system shall provide at least a visual warning signal to the driver.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o119 (same paragraph number, trigger and warning), only the page changed.

obligations.text: In case the vehicle is unexpectedly forced to become stationary during a planned manoeuvre, the system may request the driver to resume control.
obligations.reason: Permission unchanged from old o119 (same paragraph number and wording), only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.10 first sentence: indicate system-assisted manoeuvres to other road users per convention/Regulation
5.3.7.2.1.10 second sentence: use direction indicator to notify of upcoming lateral manoeuvre

obligations.text: The system shall indicate driving manoeuvres assisted by the system (e.g., a lane change or turn) to other road users as per the required convention or as specifically defined in this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as old o120 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same General Requirements parent); only page changed.

obligations.text: The system's indication of assisted manoeuvres shall include use of the direction indicator to notify road users of an upcoming lateral manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Identical second sentence in old o120 under the same parent; unchanged scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.11: ensure manoeuvre remains controllable per 5.3.6 by adapting longitudinal speed before and during manoeuvre when necessary

obligations.text: The system shall ensure the manoeuvre remains controllable for the driver, as per paragraph 5.3.6., by adapting its longitudinal speed before and during the manoeuvre when necessary.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o121 at same paragraph number and same parent (General Requirements for manoeuvres); continuity of the same scoped obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.12: manoeuvre shall aim not to cause collision with detected vehicle/road user in predicted path

obligations.text: The manoeuvre shall aim to not cause a collision with another detected vehicle or road user in the predicted path of the vehicle during the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o122 at same paragraph number and parent; o114 is a different (initiation prohibition) requirement.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.1.13: manufacturer shall describe in safety concept system behaviour when driver detected disengaged during a manoeuvre

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe in the safety concept the system behaviour in case the driver is detected to be disengaged during a manoeuvre (e.g., aborting the manoeuvre, fully executing a manoeuvre, bringing the vehicle to a safe stop).
obligations.reason: Replaces old o138 (5.3.7.2.4.3), which had the same manufacturer safety-concept description duty for driver disengagement during a manoeuvre. It now sits in the General Requirements (applying to all manoeuvres), drops 'also', and changes the examples (abort, full execution, safe stop instead of risk mitigation function).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.2 heading and applicability sentence: requirements apply to features capable of driver-initiated manoeuvres

obligations.text: The requirements of paragraph 5.3.7.2.2 and its subparagraphs apply to feature(s) capable of performing driver-initiated manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Same applicability scope statement as old o123 (same paragraph number, same wording); o125 and o134 cover different manoeuvre types.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.2.1: initiate manoeuvre only when explicitly commanded by driver without prior system request, and when safe

obligations.text: For driver-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall only initiate the manoeuvre when explicitly commanded by the driver without prior request by the system, and when it is safe to do so.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o124 at same paragraph under the same driver-initiated parent; unchanged scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3 sentence: requirements of this paragraph and subparagraphs apply to features capable of driver-confirmed manoeuvres (scope)

obligations.text: The requirements of paragraph 5.3.7.2.3 and its subparagraphs shall apply to feature(s) capable of performing driver-confirmed manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Same scoping/applicability statement as old o125 (5.3.7.2.3), identical wording and scope; same paragraph number, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.1 sentence: system designed so driver has sufficient time to confirm manoeuvre

obligations.text: For driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall be designed to ensure that the driver has sufficient time to confirm that the system may proceed with the manoeuvre, as appropriate.
obligations.reason: Replaces old o126 at the same paragraph number; the cross-reference to the requirements of 5.5.4.1.8 and subparagraphs ('In addition') was removed, while the sufficient-time requirement continues unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.2: request to confirm manoeuvre indicated by specific signal per 5.5.4.1

obligations.text: A request by the system for the driver to confirm a manoeuvre shall at least be indicated through a specific signal (or combination of signals) in accordance with paragraph 5.5.4.1.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o127 (5.3.7.2.3.2); same actor, action and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.3: system shall not initiate manoeuvre if driver does not confirm request

obligations.text: In the event that the driver does not confirm a request by the system, the system shall not initiate that manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o128 (5.3.7.2.3.3); same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.4: manoeuvre only proposed if justifiable reason

obligations.text: A manoeuvre shall only be proposed if there is a justifiable reason for said manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o129 (5.3.7.2.3.4); same scope within driver-confirmed manoeuvres.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.5 lead-in and conditions (a)-(f): system shall aim not to initiate the confirmed manoeuvre unless all listed conditions are met

obligations.text: For driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall aim not to initiate the proposed manoeuvre, even if already confirmed by the driver, unless the following conditions are met: (a) the target area, lane or path is determined by the system to be clear; (b) the reason for the manoeuvre still exists; (c) the target area or lane allows the system to resume stable control after completing the manoeuvre; (d) the manoeuvre is anticipated to be completed before the vehicle comes to standstill, unless this is necessary for safe navigation or to give way to other road users; (e) the target area or lane is assessed not to be outside of the system's boundaries; (f) the driver has been detected to have directed their gaze as appropriate to the proposed manoeuvre within an appropriate period before the manoeuvre commences.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o130 (5.3.7.2.3.5); same conditions (a)-(f) and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.6 sentence: system shall not propose a manoeuvre if it would knowingly cause other road users to unreasonably or unmanageably decelerate or evade (driver-confirmed manoeuvres)

obligations.text: For features capable of performing driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall not propose a manoeuvre if it would knowingly cause other road users to unreasonably or unmanageably decelerate or evade the vehicle as a consequence of the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number 5.3.7.2.3.6 with identical wording and the same driver-confirmed manoeuvre scope as old o131; only the page changed (11 to 12). The similar o141 is a different system-initiated scope with softer wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.7 sentence: system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would violate signage instruction or paragraph 6 performance requirements (driver-confirmed manoeuvres)

obligations.text: For features capable of performing driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would violate applicable instruction by relevant signage or performance requirements as specified in paragraph 6.
obligations.reason: Identical wording and same driver-confirmed scope as old o132 (5.3.7.2.3.7); only the page changed. The o142 candidate is the system-initiated counterpart, a different scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.3.8 sentence: system shall not propose a manoeuvre if it would lead the vehicle to cross lane markings not permitted to be crossed (driver-confirmed manoeuvres)

obligations.text: For features capable of performing driver-confirmed manoeuvres, the system shall not propose a manoeuvre if it would lead the vehicle to cross lane markings which are not permitted to be crossed.
obligations.reason: Identical wording and same driver-confirmed scope as old o133 (5.3.7.2.3.8); only the page changed. The o143 candidate is the system-initiated counterpart.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4 heading: General requirements for system-initiated manoeuvres
5.3.7.2.4 applicability sentence: requirements of this paragraph and subparagraphs apply to features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres

obligations.text: The requirements of paragraph 5.3.7.2.4 and its subparagraphs apply to feature(s) capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Identical scoping sentence and same paragraph number as old o134; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.1 first paragraph: system designed to ensure driver has sufficient time to reject announced manoeuvre in an easily accessible way, or to resume unassisted control, as appropriate
5.3.7.2.4.1 second paragraph: if driver rejects a manoeuvre, system shall not initiate the same manoeuvre unless circumstances change or imminent collision risk

obligations.text: For features performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall be designed to ensure that the driver has sufficient time to reject the manoeuvre announced by the system before it is performed in an easily accessible way, or to resume unassisted control, as appropriate.
obligations.reason: Identical text and same paragraph number 5.3.7.2.4.1 as old o135; only the page changed.

obligations.text: For features performing system-initiated manoeuvres, if the driver rejects a manoeuvre, the system shall not initiate the same manoeuvre unless the circumstances change or there is a risk of an imminent collision.
obligations.reason: Identical second paragraph within old o135 (5.3.7.2.4.1) with the same scope and exceptions.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.2 sentence: strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to initiation of the manoeuvre, documented and explained

obligations.text: For features performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the strategies shall be implemented to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to the initiation of the manoeuvre, and these strategies shall be documented and explained.
obligations.reason: Continues old o137 (5.3.7.2.4.2.1), 'further strategies... to ensure appropriate driver engagement prior to initiation, documented and explained'. It is renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.2 and the 'In addition, further' wording is dropped, which fits the old EOR 7-second rule (o136) apparently being removed or restructured. The same obligation continues with changed wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.3 first sentence: manoeuvre only performed if justifiable reason (system-initiated manoeuvres)
5.3.7.2.4.3 second sentence: manufacturer shall explain in documentation traffic situations where system may initiate manoeuvres

obligations.text: For features capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, a manoeuvre shall only be performed if there is a justifiable reason for it (e.g., pursuing a set destination, following traffic flow, safety-relevant manoeuvres, etc.).
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o139 (5.3.7.2.4.4): same actor, action, and scope (system-initiated manoeuvres, justifiable reason), identical text and same parent 5.3.7.2.4; no substantive change.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall explain in the documentation the traffic situations where the system may initiate manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o139 (5.3.7.2.4.4): same manufacturer documentation duty about traffic situations for system-initiated manoeuvres, in same parent paragraph; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.4 whole sentence: system shall not initiate manoeuvre if conditions of 5.3.7.2.3.5 not met

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall not initiate the manoeuvre if the conditions outlined in paragraph 5.3.7.2.3.5 are not met.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o140 (5.3.7.2.4.5): same system action and same cross-referenced conditions within the same parent 5.3.7.2.4; identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.5 whole sentence: system shall aim to not initiate manoeuvre causing other road users to unreasonably decelerate or evade

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would cause other road users to unreasonably or unmanageably decelerate or evade the vehicle as a consequence of the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o141 (5.3.7.2.4.6): same system-initiated scope, same 'aim to not initiate' obligation; distinct from driver-confirmed o131 which concerns proposing.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.6 whole sentence: system shall aim to not initiate manoeuvre violating signage or paragraph 6 performance requirements

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to not initiate a manoeuvre if it would violate applicable instruction by relevant signage or performance requirements as specified in paragraph 6.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o142 (5.3.7.2.4.7): same system-initiated scope and identical obligation; o132 is the driver-confirmed counterpart, not the match.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.7 whole sentence: system shall not initiate manoeuvre crossing lane markings not permitted to be crossed

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall not initiate a manoeuvre if it would lead the vehicle to cross lane markings which are not permitted to be crossed.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o143 (5.3.7.2.4.8): same system-initiated scope and identical prohibition; o133 is the driver-confirmed 'propose' counterpart.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.4.8 whole sentence: system shall aim not to violate right-of-way rules of country of operation where relevant to manoeuvre

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim not to violate appropriate right-of-way rules applicable in the country of operation where relevant to the manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Renumbered from o144 (5.3.7.2.4.9): same system-initiated manoeuvre scope and identical wording; 6.3.8 is a different context (other manoeuvres).

coverage.source_unit: Sentence 1: request for driver to acknowledge driver information material (para 5.6) given while vehicle stopped
Sentence 2: request given at least once every month
Sentence 3: extension to 3 months per user if users differentiated (permission)
Sentence 4: no repeat for driver who previously acknowledged
Sentence 5: request in current drive cycle for driver not previously acknowledged

obligations.text: For feature(s) capable of system-initiated manoeuvres, a request for the driver to acknowledge that they have read and understood the driver information material outlined in paragraph 5.6 shall be given while the vehicle is in a stopped position.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o146 (5.3.7.2.4.11), renumbered to 5.3.7.2.4.9 with the same parent paragraph; wording is identical.

obligations.text: The driver acknowledgement request shall be given at least once every month.
obligations.reason: Same monthly frequency requirement as in o146; the clause was renumbered under the same parent 5.3.7.2.4.

obligations.text: If the vehicle utilises a means of differentiating between users, the acknowledgement request interval may be extended to 3 months for a given user.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o146 ('three months' is now written '3 months'); no substantive change.

obligations.text: If the vehicle can identify that a driver has previously acknowledged the request, it does not need to be given again for that driver.
obligations.reason: Same exemption as in o146; unchanged.

obligations.text: If the vehicle can identify that the current driver has not acknowledged the request before, the request shall be given in the current drive cycle.
obligations.reason: Same requirement as in o146; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Sentence 1: notwithstanding 5.3.7.2.1.1, system-initiated manoeuvre may be initiated to mitigate risk of imminent collision (permission)
Sentence 2: DCA shall be given after manoeuvre completion once situation controllable
Sentence 3: system shall be disabled according to 5.5.4.2.8

obligations.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.3.7.2.1.1, a system-initiated manoeuvre may be initiated when it is considered to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision.
obligations.reason: Candidate o145 (5.3.7.2.4.10) covers a different requirement (highway location, HORs). o111 and o135 are related but are not the same scoped permission, so this is treated as new.

obligations.text: Following completion of a system-initiated manoeuvre performed to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision, and once the situation is controllable for the driver, a DCA shall be given.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause contains this requirement.

obligations.text: After a system-initiated manoeuvre performed to mitigate the risk of an imminent collision, the system shall be disabled according to paragraph 5.5.4.2.8.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause contains this requirement.

coverage.source_unit: Circumstances of collision-mitigation manoeuvre per 5.3.7.2.4.10 described and justified to Type Approval Authority
Circumstances assessed according to Annex 3

obligations.text: Where a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed according to paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10, the manufacturer shall describe and justify to the Type Approval Authority the circumstances in which this happens.
obligations.reason: Candidates are not equivalent: o146 is the acknowledgement request, and the others are about tolerances or documentation of different scope. This is a new scoped documentation obligation.
