obligations.text: The circumstances in which a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed according to paragraph 5.3.7.2.4.10 shall be assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause contains this Annex 3 assessment for the collision-mitigation manoeuvre.

coverage.source_unit: Heading 5.3.7.2.5 Special provisions for systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or withholding of HORs
Design obligation: anticipatory behaviour in interaction with other road users, with stable, low-amplitude dynamics and/or risk minimisation
Demonstration (a): avoid collision in lead vehicle cut-out per Annex 4 para 4.2.5.2.6
Demonstration (b): avoid collision with vehicle cutting in per Annex 4 para 4.2.5.2.5
Demonstration (c): avoid collision with decelerating lead vehicle per Annex 4 para 4.2.5.2.4

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to have anticipatory behaviour in interaction with other road user(s) aiming to ensure stable, low-amplitude dynamics and/or to minimise risk as appropriate (e.g., when critical situations could become imminent).
obligations.reason: Identical to o148 (5.3.7.2.5.1) under the same parent 5.3.7.2.5; page change only.

obligations.text: Anticipatory behaviour shall be demonstrated by avoidance of a collision in the scenario of a cut-out of the lead vehicle as outlined in Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.6, accounting for the robustness criteria outlined in Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same scenario (a) as in o148; unchanged.

obligations.text: Anticipatory behaviour shall be demonstrated by avoidance of a collision in the scenario of a vehicle cutting in from the adjacent lane as outlined in Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.5, accounting for the robustness criteria outlined in Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same scenario (b) as in o148; unchanged.

obligations.text: Anticipatory behaviour shall be demonstrated by avoidance of a collision in the scenario of a decelerating lead vehicle as outlined in Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.4, accounting for the robustness criteria outlined in Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same scenario (c) as in o148; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Whole clause: readjust following distance at next opportunity without harsh braking when distance temporarily disrupted, unless emergency manoeuvre necessary

obligations.text: In case the following distance to a vehicle in front is temporarily disrupted (e.g., vehicle cutting in, decelerating lead vehicle), the vehicle shall readjust the following distance at the next available opportunity without any harsh braking, implementing strategies aiming to address significant string instability, unless an emergency manoeuvre would become necessary.
obligations.reason: Identical to o149 (5.3.7.2.5.2) under the same parent 5.3.7.2.5; page change only.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.5.3 heading: Special provisions regarding system boundaries
5.3.7.2.5.3.1 whole sentence: highway or highway-like road operation, system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, closures, toll stations, end of highways

obligations.text: For highway or highway-like road operation, the system shall aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways (e.g., by notifying the driver, issuing a DCA, or continuing operation if capable).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old 5.3.7.2.5.3.1 (same number, same subject, same response examples); scope widened from 'highway operation' to 'highway or highway-like road operation'.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 first sentence: non-highway operation with system-initiated manoeuvres activatable, system shall aim to respond to relevant situations (stop, give way, change lane)
5.3.7.2.5.3.2 second sentence with list (a)-(d): situation within system boundaries, system manages by one of the alternatives
5.3.7.2.5.3.2 last sentence: approaching a system boundary, system shall issue a DCA

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated, the system shall aim to respond to relevant situations when the vehicle could be expected to stop, give way or required to change lane.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 (same paragraph number, same scope and wording).

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated and the relevant situation is within the system boundaries, the system shall manage it by either: (a) carrying on providing lateral and/or longitudinal assistance; or (b) suggesting a manoeuvre to the driver; or (c) issuing a DCA; or (d) performing a system-initiated manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 list (a)-(d), same scope.

obligations.text: For non-highway operation, if system-initiated manoeuvres can be activated and the relevant situation means that the system is approaching a system boundary, the system shall issue a DCA.
obligations.reason: Unchanged from old 5.3.7.2.5.3.2 final sentence, same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 whole sentence: system shall recognize lane markings per Annex 3 of UN R130 01 series, as relevant to countries of activation

obligations.text: The system shall be able to recognize lane markings as outlined in Annex 3 of the 01 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 130, as relevant to the countries in which the system can be activated.
obligations.reason: Old o152 text embeds a paragraph numbered 5.3.7.2.5.3 with identical wording; this is a renumbering to 5.3.7.2.5.3.3 of the same lane-marking obligation with unchanged scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.2.6 heading: special provisions for non-highway or HOR withholding
5.3.7.2.6.1 whole sentence: where extended testing in Annex 4 includes different VUT speeds, cover maximum operating speed in applicable test scenarios

obligations.text: For systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres in non-highway environments or during phases of withholding of HORs, where extended testing in Annex 4 includes different vehicle under test (VUT) speeds, this shall cover the maximum operating speed in the applicable test scenarios.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause contains a test-speed coverage requirement for extended Annex 4 testing; candidates concern speed limit or curvature, not test procedure scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.3 heading 'Driver Unavailability Response'
5.3.7.3.1 first sentence: driver unavailability response shall comply with UN R79 04 series RMF requirements and transitional provisions
5.3.7.3.1 second sentence: safe stop per RMF when driver determined unavailable after warning escalation sequence 5.5.4.2.6

obligations.text: The system’s driver unavailability response shall comply with the technical requirements and transitional provisions of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79 with respect to the Risk Mitigation Function (RMF).
obligations.reason: Replaces o154 first sentence (same RMF compliance obligation, same scope under 5.3.7.3.1); wording changed from 'The system' to 'The system’s driver unavailability response'.

obligations.text: In the event that the driver has been determined to be unavailable following a driver disengagement warning escalation sequence as defined in paragraph 5.5.4.2.6., the system shall come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements.
obligations.reason: Replaces o154 second sentence (same trigger, safe stop); changed from 'appropriately activate the RMF in order to come to a safe stop' to 'come to a safe stop in accordance with the RMF requirements'.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.3.2 whole clause: select appropriate target stop area

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to select an appropriate target stop area based on the system capabilities and current circumstances (e.g. traffic situation, road infrastructure) with the aim of minimising risk.
obligations.reason: Identical to o155 (5.3.7.3.2), same paragraph, same scope and wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.3.3 whole clause: where equipped with driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change, system capable of lane changes during driver unavailability response per UN R79 04 RMF, on highway toward slower/emergency lane

obligations.text: Where the system is equipped with a driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane change feature, the system shall be capable of performing lane changes during the driver unavailability response, in compliance with the technical requirements for RMF capable of bringing the vehicle to a safe stop outside its own lane of travel of the 04 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 79, during an intervention on a highway to bring the vehicle towards a target stop area in a slower or emergency lane.
obligations.reason: Replaces o156 (same paragraph number and scope: lane-change capability during RMF on highway); actor changed from 'the RMF' to 'the system' and wording reworded.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.3.4 sentence 1: permission for system-initiated manoeuvre at any time as part of driver unavailability response to mitigate risk
5.3.7.3.4 sentence 2: only after reengagement strategies failed or imminent collision risk
5.3.7.3.4 sentence 3: circumstances described and justified to Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: A system-initiated manoeuvre may be performed at any time as part of the driver unavailability response in order to mitigate risk, irrespective of the disengagement of the driver or warnings given.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; no candidate old clause covers a permission for system-initiated manoeuvres within driver unavailability response (o135 concerns rejected announced manoeuvres, different scope).

obligations.text: A system-initiated manoeuvre as part of the driver unavailability response shall only be performed after driver reengagement strategies have failed or if there is an imminent risk of collision.
obligations.reason: New restriction on system-initiated manoeuvres in the driver unavailability response; no equivalent old clause.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall describe and justify to the Type Approval Authority the circumstances in which a system-initiated manoeuvre is performed as part of the driver unavailability response.
obligations.reason: New documentation/justification obligation specific to this scope; o287 and o261 are different subjects (warning counts, gaze aversion).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4 heading 'Speed Limit Compliance Assistance'
5.3.7.4.1 - system shall aim to determine permitted road speed limit relevant to current lane of travel

obligations.text: The system shall aim to determine the permitted road speed limit relevant to the current lane of travel.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording and scope as old o158 (Speed Limit Compliance Assistance); only page shifted from 13 to 14.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.2 - system shall continuously display the system-determined road speed limit to the driver

obligations.text: The system shall continuously display the system-determined road speed limit to the driver.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o159 in the same section; same actor, action and object, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.3 - system and any of its features shall only provide assistance within designed speed range

obligations.text: The system and any of its features shall only provide assistance within their designed speed range.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o160 in the same section; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.4 - maximum speed up to which system and features provide assistance shall not exceed country maximum speed limit

obligations.text: The maximum speed up to which the system and any of its features provides assistance shall not exceed the maximum speed limit in the country where the vehicle is currently operating.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o161 in the same section; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.5 - current maximum speed determined from (a) driver-set maximum speed or (b) system-determined road speed limit

obligations.text: The current maximum speed the system may assist up to shall be determined either from (a) the driver-set maximum speed or (b) the system-determined road speed limit.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o162 including alternatives (a) and (b); same scope, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.6 - system shall automatically control vehicle speed to not exceed current maximum speed

obligations.text: The system shall automatically control the vehicle speed to not exceed the current maximum speed.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o163 in the same section; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7 – system shall provide means for driver to set driver-set maximum speed within designed speed range

obligations.text: The system shall provide a means for the driver to set a driver-set maximum speed within the system's designed speed range.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as o164 (identical wording, same paragraph number 5.3.7.4.7 under same parent 5.3.7.4); only page shifted from 13 to 15.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.1 – when vehicle speed exceeds system-determined road speed limit, provide at least optical signal for appropriate duration

obligations.text: When the vehicle speed exceeds the system-determined road speed limit, the system shall provide at least an optical signal to the driver for an appropriate duration.
obligations.reason: Matches o165: same paragraph number, same trigger (speed exceeding limit), same action (optical signal) and same parent 5.3.7.4.7; unchanged apart from page.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.2 – system may incorporate feature allowing driver to confirm or reject change in current maximum speed before automatic change

obligations.text: The system may incorporate a feature allowing the driver to confirm or reject any change in the current maximum speed before it is automatically changed by the system.
obligations.reason: Matches o166: identical permission, same paragraph number and parent context; unchanged apart from page.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.3 – introductory sentence: in case of change in system-determined road speed limit the following shall apply
coverage.exclusion_reason: Introductory/lead-in sentence that only sets the shared condition for sub-paragraphs 5.3.7.4.7.3.1 to .3.4; it has no independent obligation, and the obligations are extracted in the sub-clauses.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.3.1 – driver shall be given at least acoustic or haptic signal, which may be suppressed permanently by driver (on change in road speed limit)

obligations.text: In the case of a change in the system-determined road speed limit, the driver shall be given at least an acoustic or haptic signal, which may be suppressed permanently by the driver.
obligations.reason: Matches o168: same paragraph number, same parent 5.3.7.4.7.3 scope (speed limit change), identical signal requirement and suppression permission.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.3.2 – if current max speed was driver-set and lower than both previous and new system-determined limits, it shall not automatically change to new limit

obligations.text: In the case of a change in the system-determined road speed limit, if the current maximum speed before the change was a driver-set maximum speed and it is lower than both the previous and the new system-determined road speed limit, the current maximum speed shall not automatically change to the new system-determined road speed limit.
obligations.reason: Matches o169: identical conditions and constraint, same paragraph number and parent scope; unchanged apart from page.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.3.3 whole sentence: if new system-determined road speed limit is lower than current maximum speed, current maximum speed automatically changes to the new limit

obligations.text: When the system-determined road speed limit changes and the new limit is lower than the current maximum speed, the system shall automatically change the current maximum speed to the new system-determined road speed limit.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o170 (same paragraph number 5.3.7.4.7.3.3 under the same parent 5.3.7.4.7.3 about speed limit change); wording and scope are identical, only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.7.3.4 manufacturer shall document system behaviour for cases not addressed in change of system-determined road speed limit, and demonstrate to Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: For cases not specifically addressed by the provisions of 5.3.7.4.7.3, the manufacturer shall document the system behaviour in response to a change in system-determined road speed limit and demonstrate this to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o171 (same paragraph number and parent 5.3.7.4.7.3); identical scope and actor, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.8 whole sentence: system-initiated speed change due to changed road speed limit shall be controllable by driver

obligations.text: Any system-initiated change in vehicle speed due to a changed system-determined road speed limit shall be controllable by the driver.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o172 (same paragraph 5.3.7.4.8, same parent 5.3.7.4); unchanged wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.9 whole sentence: system shall not enable driver to set default offset exceeding system-determined road speed limit

obligations.text: The system shall not enable the driver to set a default offset by which the current maximum speed is supposed to exceed the system-determined road speed limit.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o173 (same paragraph 5.3.7.4.9, same parent); unchanged wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.10 permission to apply technically reasonable tolerances to warning thresholds and designed speed range, and requirement that they be declared by manufacturer to Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: Technically reasonable tolerances (e.g., related to speedometer inaccuracy) may be applied to the warning thresholds and the system's designed speed range, and shall be declared by the manufacturer to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o174 (same paragraph 5.3.7.4.10, same parent); identical wording and scope. The permission and declaration duty are one conditional obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.4.11 provisions of 5.3.7.4 shall not prejudice national or regional legislation regulating speed limit control systems

obligations.text: The provisions of paragraph 5.3.7.4 shall not be in prejudice to any national or regional legislation which regulates the speed limit control system.
obligations.reason: Same scoped compliance provision as old o175 (same paragraph 5.3.7.4.11, same parent); unchanged wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.5. Safe Headway Assistance (heading only)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; imposes no obligation itself.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.5.1 The system shall support the driver in complying with regulatorily defined headway according to national traffic rules.

obligations.text: The system shall support the driver in complying with regulatorily defined headway according to national traffic rules.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o177 (5.3.7.5.1) under the same parent Safe Headway Assistance; identical actor, action and scope, only page changed (14 to 15).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.5.1.1 For M1 and N1 vehicles, requirement 5.3.7.5.1 deemed fulfilled if either of the following requirements are met (deemed-compliance condition)

obligations.text: For M1 and N1 vehicles, the requirement in paragraph 5.3.7.5.1 (support the driver in complying with regulatorily defined headway) shall be deemed fulfilled if either of the following requirements (5.3.7.5.1.1.1 or 5.3.7.5.1.1.2) is met.
obligations.reason: Matches old clause o178 (5.3.7.5.1.1): same M1/N1 scope, same deemed-compliance relation to 5.3.7.5.1; only relocated by page.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.5.1.1.1 System shall permanently indicate current headway setting while in 'active' mode

obligations.text: For M1 and N1 vehicles (as an option for deemed fulfilment of 5.3.7.5.1), the system shall permanently indicate to the driver the current headway setting while the system is in 'active' mode.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o179 (5.3.7.5.1.1.1) under the same parent; wording unchanged, only page differs.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.7.5.1.1.2 Upon first activation following powertrain initiation, inform driver if headway configuration is lower than 2 seconds
Footnote 3 definition of powertrain initiation reference (M.R.2)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Footnote reference to a definition; not a separate obligation.

obligations.text: For M1 and N1 vehicles (as an option for deemed fulfilment of 5.3.7.5.1), upon first activation of the system following an initiation of the powertrain, the system shall provide information to the driver that the headway configuration is set to a value lower than 2 seconds, if that is the case.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o180 (5.3.7.5.1.1.2) with identical condition, value (2 s) and parent; only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4 System safety response to detected failures (heading only)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; imposes no obligation itself.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.1 whole sentence: activated system capable of detecting and responding to electrical and non-electrical failure conditions

obligations.text: The activated system shall be capable of detecting and responding to electrical and non-electrical (e.g., sensor blockage, misalignment) failure conditions affecting the safe operation of the system or its features.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o182 (5.4.1) under the same parent 5.4; identical wording, actor, and scope; only the page changed (14 to 16).

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.2 first sentence: upon failure detection, terminate control assistance of affected feature(s)/system safely per manufacturer's safety concept
5.4.2 second sentence: gradually reduce control assistance if safe, and inform driver per 5.5.4.1

obligations.text: Upon detection of a failure affecting the safe operation of a given feature(s) or the system as a whole, the control assistance of the affected feature(s) or the system altogether shall be terminated in a safe manner in accordance with the manufacturer's safety concept.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o183 (5.4.2, first sentence) under the same parent 5.4; identical scope and wording, with only the page changed.

obligations.text: The system shall gradually reduce its control assistance provided by the affected feature(s) or system if it is safe to do so, and inform the driver according to paragraph 5.5.4.1.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o183 (5.4.2, second sentence); unchanged text and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.2.1 whole: if failure affects entire system, switch to 'off' mode upon termination and provide at least an optical failure warning for an appropriate duration

obligations.text: If a failure affects the entire system, the system shall switch to 'off' mode upon termination of assistance and provide at least an optical failure warning signal to the driver for an appropriate duration.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o184 (5.4.2.1) under the same parent 5.4.2; identical wording and scope; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.2.2 whole: failure affecting system indicated to driver with at least an optical signal unless system is in 'off' mode

obligations.text: The failure affecting the system shall be indicated to the driver with at least an optical signal unless the system is in 'off' mode.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o185 (5.4.2.2) under the same parent 5.4.2; identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.3 whole: manufacturer shall take appropriate measures per 5.3.6 to ensure failures remain controllable by the driver

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall take appropriate measures (according to paragraph 5.3.6.) to ensure that failures in the system remain controllable by the driver.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o186 (5.4.3) under the same parent 5.4; identical wording, actor, and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.4 whole: permission to continue operation if failure affects only some features, provided remaining features operate per this Regulation

obligations.text: If a failure only affects some features, the system operation is permitted to continue provided that the remaining features are capable of operating in accordance to this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same conditional permission as old o187 (5.4.4) under the same parent 5.4; identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.4.1 – remaining available features or absence of features after a failure shall be visually indicated to driver in an easily understandable manner

obligations.text: Where a failure affects only some features, the system shall visually indicate to the driver, in an easily understandable manner, the remaining available features or the absence of those features as a result of the failure.
obligations.reason: Same scoped HMI obligation as old 5.4.4.1 under the same parent 5.4.4 (failure affecting only some features); text identical, only the page changed from 14 to 16.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.4.2 first sentence – manufacturer shall describe which features can operate independently if the system can continue assistance after a failure disabling a feature
5.4.4.2 second sentence – this shall be assessed according to Annex 3

obligations.text: If the system is able to provide continued assistance in the case of a failure disabling a given feature, the manufacturer shall describe which features are able to operate independently from one another.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.4.4.2 (o189) with the same parent 5.4.4 and the same actor, condition and action; only the page changed.

obligations.text: The description of which features are able to operate independently from one another (where the system can continue assistance after a failure disabling a given feature) shall be assessed according to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: The Annex 3 assessment requirement is in old 5.4.4.2 (o189) with the same scope and wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.5 – system shall notify driver of the failure and unavailability when driver attempts to switch to 'on' mode a system or feature unavailable due to a failure

obligations.text: When the driver attempts to switch to 'on' mode the system or a feature that is unavailable due to a failure, the system shall provide a notice to the driver about the failure and the unavailability of the system or given feature.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.4.5 (o190) with the same applicability condition and action; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5 heading – Human-Machine Interface (HMI)
5.5.1 heading and introductory line for the diagram of DCAS modes of operation
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading and diagram introduction only; no stand-alone obligation in the supplied text.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2 heading – General Requirements
5.5.2.1 – when system switched into 'on' mode, specific features shall be in 'active' or 'stand-by' mode
5.5.2.1 – some other features may remain in 'off' mode and be commanded by different means (permission)

obligations.text: When the system is switched into 'on' mode, specific system features shall be either in 'active' mode (generating control outputs) or in 'stand-by' mode (currently not generating control outputs).
obligations.reason: Same scoped requirement as old o194 (5.5.2.1), identical wording and same paragraph number, same section context; only page changed.

obligations.text: When the system is switched into 'on' mode, some other system features may remain in 'off' mode and be commanded by a different means.
obligations.reason: Permission matches the same sentence in old o194 (5.5.2.1); same actor, scope and condition, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2.2 – when system switched to 'off' by driver, no automatic transition to any system providing continuous longitudinal and/or lateral movement

obligations.text: When the system is switched to 'off' mode by the driver, there shall not be an automatic transition to any system which provides continuous longitudinal and/or lateral movement of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o195 (5.5.2.2), same paragraph, same scope; relocated page only.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2.3 – in 'active' mode, no other system than DCAS provides sustained longitudinal and lateral control, unless emergency safety system intervention per paragraph 5.2

obligations.text: When the system is in 'active' mode, sustained longitudinal and lateral control assistance shall not be provided by any other system other than DCAS, unless an intervention of an emergency safety system is deemed necessary as specified in paragraph 5.2.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o196 (5.5.2.3), same paragraph and scope including the emergency exception.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2.4 – HMI designed not to cause mode confusion with other systems on the vehicle

obligations.text: The HMI shall be designed not to cause mode confusion with other systems equipped on the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o197 (5.5.2.4), same paragraph and scope; not equivalent to the more general o223 message clarity clause.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2.4.1 – DCAS-dedicated vehicle controls clearly identified and distinguishable, without prejudice to UN R121
5.5.2.4.1 – last sentence: aim to promote correct use, not intended to prohibit multifunction controls
coverage.exclusion_reason: Statement of intent/clarification of the requirement, not a separate obligation; preserved in the obligation text.

obligations.text: Without prejudice to the provisions of UN Regulation No. 121, the vehicle controls dedicated to the DCAS shall be clearly identified and distinguishable (e.g., through size, form, colour, type, action, spacing and/or control shape) to accommodate only the appropriate interactions; this is intended to promote correct use and does not prohibit multifunction controls.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o198 (5.5.2.4.1), same paragraph, same scope and exceptions.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3 – heading 'Activation, Deactivation and Driver Override'
5.5.3.1 first sentence: default status 'off' mode at each initiation of the powertrain regardless of previously selected driver mode
5.5.3.1 second paragraph: automatic engine start (e.g. stop/start) not considered 'initiation of the powertrain'

obligations.text: The default status of the system shall be the 'off' mode at each initiation of the powertrain, regardless of what mode the driver had previously selected.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o200 (5.5.3.1), identical wording, same paragraph number, same parent 5.5.3; moved only by page shift.

obligations.text: A new engine start (or run cycle) performed automatically, e.g. by a stop/start system, shall not be considered an 'initiation of the powertrain' wherever that term is used in this regulation.
obligations.reason: Same interpretive rule as in old o200 5.5.3.1 second paragraph, unchanged in scope and wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.2 heading 'Activation'
5.5.3.2.1: at the latest when system first enters 'active' mode after powertrain initiation, provide visual information requesting driver to remain engaged

obligations.text: At the latest when the system first enters 'active' mode following an initiation of the powertrain, the system shall provide visual information to the driver requesting them to remain engaged with the driving task while using the system.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o202 (5.5.3.2.1) under the same Activation parent; same actor, trigger and action.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.2.2: mode change from 'off' to 'on' only upon deliberate driver action

obligations.text: The system shall change its mode from 'off' to 'on' only upon a deliberate action of the driver.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o203 (5.5.3.2.2), same scope and parent.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.2.3 intro and list (a)-(e): system or features enter 'active' mode only if all preconditions are met
5.5.3.2.3 final paragraph: manufacturer shall specify additional preconditions in documentation, if applicable

obligations.text: The system or its features shall only enter 'active' mode if all of the following conditions are met: (a) the driver is in the driver seat and the driver's safety belt is fastened; (b) the system is able to monitor the driver's potential disengagement with the driving task; (c) no failure affecting the safe operation of the system has been detected; (d) the system or feature has not detected to be outside of its system boundaries; (e) other safety systems according to paragraph 5.2 are functional.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o204 (5.5.3.2.3) precondition list; same scope.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall specify in the documentation additional types of preconditions enabling the system or its features to enter 'active' mode, if applicable.
obligations.reason: Same documentation obligation as in old o204 (5.5.3.2.3 final paragraph), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.3 heading 'Deactivation'
5.5.3.3.1 whole sentence: driver able to switch system to 'off' mode at any time

obligations.text: It shall be possible for the driver to switch the system to 'off' mode at any time.
obligations.reason: Identical scoped obligation to old o206 (5.5.3.3.1, Deactivation, same parent context); only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.3.2 whole sentence: when driver switches system or feature off, it shall go to 'off' mode

obligations.text: When the driver switches the system or one of its features off, the system or feature respectively shall go to 'off' mode.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o207 (5.5.3.3.2, Deactivation); unchanged wording and context, renumbered page only.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.3.3 whole sentence: on loss of preconditions for 'active' mode, terminate control output safely and timely via 'stand-by' or 'off', unless otherwise defined by the Regulation

obligations.text: When the system or a feature thereof has assessed that the preconditions for remaining in 'active' mode are no longer met, the system or features shall terminate the control output in a safe and timely manner by either transitioning to 'stand-by' mode or by switching the system or feature to 'off' mode, unless specifically defined otherwise by this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o208 (5.5.3.3.3, Deactivation); identical wording and context.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.3.4 whole sentence: no resumption of longitudinal control without driver input after standstill following emergency safety system intervention

obligations.text: The system shall not resume longitudinal control without driver input if the vehicle comes to a standstill following an intervention by an emergency safety system (e.g., AEBS).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o209 (5.5.3.3.4, Deactivation); identical wording and context.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4 heading 'Driver Override'
5.5.3.4.1 whole sentence: system or feature may remain in 'active' mode provided priority is given to driver input during overriding period

obligations.text: The system or feature may remain in 'active' mode, provided that priority is given to the driver input during the overriding period.
obligations.reason: Same scoped permission/condition as old o211 (5.5.3.4.1, Driver Override); identical wording and context.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.1 whole sentence: driver braking input with higher deceleration than system overrides and suspends longitudinal control assistance during overriding period

obligations.text: A driver input to the braking control resulting in a higher deceleration than that induced by the system shall override and suspend the longitudinal control assistance provided by the system during the overriding period.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording and scope as old clause o212 (driver braking override); same parent context, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.1.1 first sentence, mandatory part: system shall not resume longitudinal control assistance without separate driver action
5.5.3.4.1.1.1 first sentence, permission: system may provide longitudinal assistance to avoid inappropriate distances to other road users
5.5.3.4.1.1.1 second sentence: permission to resume without separate action if speed reduction not more than 30 km/h within 2 s

obligations.text: After a driver override of longitudinal control assistance by braking input, the system shall not resume longitudinal control assistance without a separate action by the driver.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o213 (same paragraph number, same scope, same parent 5.5.3.4.1.1); only page changed.

obligations.text: Notwithstanding the prohibition on resuming without a separate driver action, the system may provide longitudinal control assistance in order to avoid inappropriate distances to other road users.
obligations.reason: Same permission in old o213 with identical wording and context.

obligations.text: If the driver input results in a speed reduction of not more than 30 km/h within 2 seconds, the system may resume longitudinal control assistance without a separate action by the driver.
obligations.reason: Same permission and values (30 km/h, 2 s) as old o213, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.1.2 first sentence: following resumption the system may accelerate up to the current maximum speed
5.5.3.4.1.1.2 second sentence: rate of increase of acceleration gradual (low jerk) and controllable per 5.3.6

obligations.text: Following resumption of longitudinal control assistance, the system may accelerate up to the current maximum speed.
obligations.reason: Identical permission to old o214 under the same parent; only page changed.

obligations.text: Following resumption of longitudinal control assistance, the rate of increase of acceleration shall be gradual (i.e. with low jerk) and controllable in accordance with paragraph 5.3.6.
obligations.reason: Identical requirement to old o214, same scope and cross-reference.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.2 whole sentence: driver input to any braking system to maintain standstill overrides longitudinal control assistance

obligations.text: A driver input to the control of any braking system (e.g., service brake, parking brake) in order to maintain the vehicle at standstill shall override the longitudinal control assistance performed by the system.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o215 with same paragraph number and scope; only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.3 first sentence: accelerator input with higher acceleration than system overrides longitudinal control assistance
5.5.3.4.1.3 second sentence: system shall resume longitudinal control on basis of current maximum speed

obligations.text: An accelerator input by the driver with a higher acceleration than that induced by the system shall override longitudinal control assistance provided by the system.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o216, same paragraph and scope.

obligations.text: After an accelerator-input override, the system shall resume longitudinal control assistance on the basis of the current maximum speed.
obligations.reason: Identical resumption requirement in old o216, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.4 first sentence: steering input overrides any lateral control assistance feature
5.5.3.4.1.4 second sentence: override steering effort shall not exceed 50 N
5.5.3.4.1.4 third sentence: system may allow minor lateral corrections

obligations.text: A steering input by the driver shall override any feature associated with the lateral control assistance performed by the system.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o217, same paragraph and scope.

obligations.text: The steering control effort necessary for the driver to override lateral control assistance shall not exceed 50 N.
obligations.reason: Same 50 N limit as old o217, unchanged.

obligations.text: The system may allow the driver to perform minor lateral corrections (e.g. to avoid a pothole).
obligations.reason: Same permission as old o217, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.4.1 main clause: terminate manoeuvre on driver override unless steering supports manoeuvre or is minor lateral correction

obligations.text: When driver override occurs while the system is performing a manoeuvre, the manoeuvre shall be terminated unless the steering input is in support of the intended manoeuvre and/or providing minor lateral corrections.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording as o218 with the same parent context (5.5.3.4.1.4). Only the page changed, so this is a continuation of the same scoped obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.3.4.1.5 main clause: if system no longer permitted to provide assistance in response to driver override (per 5.3.7.4.4), design to ensure controllability

obligations.text: If according to paragraph 5.3.7.4.4 the system is no longer permitted to provide longitudinal or lateral assistance in response to driver override, the system shall be designed to ensure controllability of these phases of operation (e.g. not terminating lateral control while the driver is detected to be motorically disengaged).
obligations.reason: Identical wording and paragraph number as o219 under the same parent context. Only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4 heading: Driver Information, Driver Disengagement and Warning Strategies
5.5.4.1 heading: Driver Information
5.5.4.1.1 intro with items (a)-(g): inform or warn the driver about system status, manoeuvre status, driver action need, system boundary, upcoming boundary, failures, intended manoeuvres
5.5.4.1.1 (h): basis for the system being disabled due to insufficient engagement
5.5.4.1.1 (i): basis for why a DCA has been issued if not addressed above or if it follows an engagement request escalation

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about: (a) the status of the system or feature: 'stand-by' mode (if applicable), 'active' mode; (b) status of an ongoing manoeuvre (e.g. initiation, cancellation or if it will be recommenced after the vehicle is forced to come to a stop during the manoeuvre); (c) the need for the driver to perform a specific action (e.g. apply control, check indirect vision devices); (d) if while in 'active' mode the system has detected to have reached a currently relevant system boundary, unless already indicated by (a); (e) a detected upcoming system boundary; (f) detected failures affecting the system or its features, unless the system is in 'off' mode; (g) intended driver-confirmed or system-initiated manoeuvres.
obligations.reason: Items (a)-(g) are identical to o222 (same paragraph 5.5.4.1.1, same parent 5.5.4.1), so this is the same scoped obligation.

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the basis for the system being disabled due to insufficient engagement.
obligations.reason: Item (h) does not appear in candidate o222, which ends at (g). No other candidate covers this information requirement, so it is a new obligation.

obligations.text: The system shall inform or warn the driver about the basis for why a DCA has been issued, if not addressed by items (a)-(h) of 5.5.4.1.1 or if it follows an engagement request escalation.
obligations.reason: Item (i) does not appear in candidate o222, which ends at (g). No other candidate covers it, so it is a new obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.2 system messages and signals shall be unambiguous, timely and not lead to confusion

obligations.text: The system messages and signals shall be unambiguous, timely and shall not lead to confusion.
obligations.reason: Identical wording and paragraph number as o223 under the same parent 5.5.4.1. Only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.3 – messages and signals use individual or appropriate combination of visual, audio and/or haptic feedback

obligations.text: The system's messages and signals shall use individual or an appropriate combination of visual, audio and/or haptic feedback for the given circumstances.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number 5.5.4.1.3 with identical wording, actor, object and scope as the old clause under the same parent 5.5.4.1; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.4 sentence 1 – multiple parallel messages/signals prioritized by urgency
5.5.4.1.4 sentence 2 – safety-relevant messages and signals given greatest urgency
5.5.4.1.4 sentence 3 – manufacturer lists and explains all messages and signals in documentation

obligations.text: In the case of multiple messages or signals being offered in parallel, they shall be subject to prioritization by urgency.
obligations.reason: Identical text in the same paragraph number and parent as old clause o225; same scope and continuity.

obligations.text: Where multiple messages or signals are offered in parallel, safety-relevant messages and signals shall be given the greatest urgency.
obligations.reason: Identical sentence in the same paragraph of old clause o225; unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall list and explain all system messages and signals in the documentation.
obligations.reason: Identical manufacturer documentation obligation in the same paragraph of old clause o225; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.5 – messages and signals designed to actively encourage driver understanding of system state, capabilities, and driver tasks and responsibilities

obligations.text: The system's messages and signals shall be designed to actively encourage driver understanding of the state of the system, its capabilities and the driver's tasks and responsibilities.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording as old clause o226 under the same parent; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.6 – messages and signals encourage driver understanding of intended control outputs

obligations.text: The system's messages and signals shall encourage driver understanding of the system's intended control outputs.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording as old clause o227 under the same parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.7 – overall status indication unambiguously distinguishable from any ADS status indication

obligations.text: The system's overall status indication shall be unambiguously distinguishable from the status indication of any ADS equipped on the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording as old clause o228 under the same parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.8 – heading 'System Messages and Signals for Driver-Confirmed Manoeuvres'
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; contains no independent obligation.

coverage.source_unit: Sentence 1: system shall visually inform driver about a proposed manoeuvre
Sentence 2: series of manoeuvres shall be comprehensible, connected series
Sentence 3: manufacturer shall explain timing to Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: The system shall visually inform the driver about a proposed manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: Same wording and scope as old 5.5.4.1.8.1 under same parent 5.5.4.1.8 (Driver-Confirmed Manoeuvres); renumbering/page shift only.

obligations.text: If informing the driver about a series of manoeuvres, the visual information shall be a combination that is comprehensible to the driver and of a connected series.
obligations.reason: Same conditional requirement as old o230 in same paragraph and parent; unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall explain to the Type Approval Authority the timing at which the visual manoeuvre information is provided to ensure appropriate driver response.
obligations.reason: Same manufacturer documentation obligation as old o230; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Single sentence: direction indicators not deemed to satisfy requirement

obligations.text: The direction indicators shall not be deemed to satisfy the requirement to visually inform the driver about proposed manoeuvres (5.5.4.1.8).
obligations.reason: Identical to old o231 under same parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Single sentence: signals and messages designed to avoid overreliance or misuse

obligations.text: The system's signals and messages shall be designed to avoid driver overreliance or misuse.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o232 under same parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Heading: System Messages and Signals for System-Initiated Manoeuvres
Single sentence: provisions of 5.5.4.1.8 shall equally apply to system-initiated manoeuvres

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the provisions of 5.5.4.1.8 shall equally apply.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o234 under same parent 5.5.4.1.9; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Sentence 1: aim to provide visual information at least 3 s ahead or with sufficient notice
Sentence 2: time may be reduced if imminent collision or conflict; inform as far in advance as possible
Sentence 3: if notice less than 3 s, manufacturer shall provide evidence

obligations.text: For system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall aim to provide the visual information at least 3 seconds ahead of the initiation of a relevant intended manoeuvre or with sufficient notice to allow the driver to comprehend the manoeuvre and the traffic situation, taking into account the complexity of the manoeuvre and the amount of other road users present.
obligations.reason: Replaces old o235 first sentence; adds the explicit 'at least 3 seconds' target and 'visual' qualifier to the same advance-notice obligation.

obligations.text: If there is a risk of imminent collision or the information would conflict with information about an ongoing manoeuvre, the notice time may be reduced and the system shall visually inform the driver as far in advance as possible.
obligations.reason: Same exception and requirement as in old o235 second sentence; unchanged.

obligations.text: Where the visual notice is less than 3 seconds ahead of initiation, the manufacturer shall provide evidence to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that the timing ensures an appropriate driver response and that the strategies employed ensure drivers notice the information without undue delay.
obligations.reason: New manufacturer evidence obligation for notice under 3 s; not in old o235.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.9.3 sentence: where system can perform system-initiated manoeuvres, system shall indicate to driver whether manoeuvres could be initiated automatically or only upon driver initiation/confirmation

obligations.text: Provided the system is capable of performing system-initiated manoeuvres, the system shall indicate to the driver whether, in the current mode of operation, manoeuvres could be initiated automatically, or only upon driver initiation or confirmation.
obligations.reason: Renumbered/relocated identical paragraph with same paragraph number 5.5.4.1.9.3 under same parent 5.5.4.1.9; same actor, action and condition as o236.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.1.9.4 first sentence: system shall offer driver the possibility to visualize at least a representation of the intended manoeuvre
5.5.4.1.9.4 second sentence: visualization shall aim not to cause unnecessary distraction

obligations.text: The system shall offer the driver the possibility to visualize at least a representation of the intended manoeuvre (system messages and signals for system-initiated manoeuvres).
obligations.reason: New paragraph; candidates (o119 warning on stationary vehicle, o230 visual information on proposed driver-confirmed manoeuvre) differ in scope and action; no positive evidence of continuity.

obligations.text: The visualization of the intended manoeuvre shall aim to not cause unnecessary distraction to the driver.
obligations.reason: Distinct design constraint on the visualization for system-initiated manoeuvres; no equivalent in the candidates.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2 sentence: driver state monitoring system and warning strategy shall be documented and demonstrated by manufacturer to TAA during safety concept inspection per Annex 3 and relevant Annex 4 tests

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document and demonstrate the driver state monitoring system and its warning strategy to the Type Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3 and according to the relevant tests of Annex 4.
obligations.reason: Identical text with same paragraph number 5.5.4.2 and same parent; matches o237.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.1 heading: Driver Disengagement Monitoring
5.5.4.2.1 sentence: system shall be equipped with means to appropriately detect driver disengagement as specified in following paragraphs

obligations.text: The system shall be equipped with means to appropriately detect driver disengagement as specified in the following paragraphs.
obligations.reason: Identical text with same paragraph number and parent; matches o238.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.1.1: system shall monitor whether driver is motorically (5.5.4.2.4) and visually (5.5.4.2.5) disengaged

obligations.text: The system shall monitor if the driver is motorically (as per paragraph 5.5.4.2.4.) and visually (as per paragraph 5.5.4.2.5.) disengaged.
obligations.reason: Identical text with same paragraph number and parent; matches o239.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.1.2: if visual disengagement determination is temporarily unavailable, system shall not lead vehicle to leave its current lane

obligations.text: If visual disengagement determination is detected to be temporarily unavailable, the system shall not lead the vehicle to leave its current lane of travel.
obligations.reason: Identical text with same paragraph number and parent; matches o240.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.2 heading: General Requirements for Driver Disengagement Warnings
5.5.4.2.2.1 warning shall guide driver on required actions to support engagement in driving task

obligations.text: The driver disengagement warning shall guide the driver on the required actions in order to support appropriate engagement in the driving task.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording and scope as old 5.5.4.2.2.1 under the same parent chain; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.2.2 warning and escalation strategy shall consider and prioritize warning strategies of simultaneously activated emergency assistance systems (e.g. AEBS)

obligations.text: The system's warning and escalation strategy shall consider for and prioritize warning strategies of simultaneously activated emergency assistance systems (e.g. AEBS).
obligations.reason: Renumbered from old 5.5.4.2.2.3 (o243): same actor, action and object (warning/escalation strategy prioritizing emergency assistance system warnings) under the same parent 5.5.4.2.2; wording identical, so a relocation rather than a new obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3 heading: Types of Warnings
5.5.4.2.3.1 heading: Hands On Request (HOR)
5.5.4.2.3.1.1 HOR shall contain at least continual (continuous or intermittent) visual information similar to example

obligations.text: A Hands On Request (HOR) shall contain at least a continual (continuous or intermittent) visual information similar to the example presented below.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording and scope as old 5.5.4.2.3.1.1 under the same HOR parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3.1.2 – HOR considered confirmed, as a minimum, when driver is no longer motorically disengaged

obligations.text: An HOR shall, as a minimum, be considered confirmed when the driver is no longer motorically disengaged.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording and scope (HOR confirmation criterion) as old clause o247; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3.2 – heading 'Eyes On Request (EOR)'
5.5.4.2.3.2.1 – EOR shall be continual visual information combined with at least one other modality, clear and easily perceptible, unless it is ensured the driver has observed the visual information

obligations.text: An EOR shall be a continual visual information in combination with at least one other modality, which are clear and easily perceptible, unless it can be ensured that the driver has observed the visual information.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number and wording, same EOR design requirement, as old clause o249; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3.2.2 – EOR considered confirmed, as a minimum, when driver is no longer visually disengaged per 5.5.4.2.5

obligations.text: An EOR shall, as a minimum, be considered confirmed when the driver is no longer visually disengaged as per paragraph 5.5.4.2.5.
obligations.reason: Identical paragraph number, wording and scope (EOR confirmation criterion) as old clause o250; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3.3 – heading 'Direct Control Alert (DCA)'
5.5.4.2.3.3.1 first sentence – DCA shall clearly and prominently instruct driver to immediately resume at least lateral control
5.5.4.2.3.3.1 second sentence – DCA shall comprise a visual warning combined with at least one other modality, clear and easily perceptible

obligations.text: A DCA shall clearly and prominently instruct the driver to immediately resume at least lateral control of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical DCA content instruction as old clause o252; only the page changed.

obligations.text: A DCA shall comprise a visual warning combined with at least one other modality, which are clear and easily perceptible.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical DCA modality requirement as old clause o252; only the page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.3.3.2 DCA confirmation criterion (minimum: driver has taken control without continuous lateral assistance requested by DCA)

obligations.text: A DCA shall, as a minimum, be considered confirmed when the driver has taken control of the vehicle without any continuous lateral assistance as requested by the DCA.
obligations.reason: Same scoped DCA confirmation criterion as o253 (5.5.4.2.3.3.2) under the same DCA parent; text identical and only the page changed (19 to 21), so this is a relocation without substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.4 heading 'Assessment of Motoric Disengagement'
5.5.4.2.4.1 deemed motorically disengaged when driver has removed hands from steering control

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to be motorically disengaged when the driver has removed their hands from the steering control.
obligations.reason: Identical to o255 (5.5.4.2.4.1) with the same parent, Assessment of Motoric Disengagement; same scope, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.5 heading 'Assessment of Visual Disengagement'
5.5.4.2.5.1 first sentence: DSM shall detect visual disengagement at minimum based on eye gaze detection
5.5.4.2.5.1 second sentence: head posture may also be used if eye gaze temporarily cannot be determined or head posture determines disengagement more quickly (permission)

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system shall detect the driver's visual disengagement at a minimum based on the detection of the driver's eye gaze.
obligations.reason: Identical to the first sentence of o257 (5.5.4.2.5.1) under the same parent; same actor and scope.

obligations.text: The driver state monitoring system may also use head posture to detect visual disengagement if the driver's eye gaze can temporarily not be determined, or where the head posture can determine the disengagement more quickly.
obligations.reason: Same permission as the second sentence of o257 (5.5.4.2.5.1); unchanged wording and conditions.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.5.2 para 1: driver deemed visually disengaged when gaze/head posture directed away from any driving task relevant area
5.5.4.2.5.2 para 2 first sentence: manufacturer shall specify outline of driving task relevant areas and when relevant in documentation to TAA
5.5.4.2.5.2 para 2 second sentence: dashboard/instrument panel may be considered relevant only while manoeuvre relevant information displayed, max 3 s
5.5.4.2.5.2 para 3: EOR warning time shall not be extended by gaze time toward dashboard/instrument panel

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed to be visually disengaged when the driver's eye gaze and/or head posture, as relevant, is directed away from any currently driving task relevant area.
obligations.reason: Same definition as the first paragraph of o258 (5.5.4.2.5.2), unchanged.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall specify, in the documentation provided to the Type Approval Authority, an outline of the driving task relevant areas and when they are relevant.
obligations.reason: Same documentation obligation as the second paragraph, first sentence of o258; unchanged.

obligations.text: For the assessment of visual disengagement, the dashboard and instrument panel may be considered a driving task relevant area only while manoeuvre relevant information (as detailed in paragraph 5.5.4.1.8.1. or 5.5.4.1.9.4.) is displayed, for a maximum duration of 3 seconds.
obligations.reason: Replaces the o258 rule that the dashboard and instrument panel shall not be considered a driving task relevant area with a limited exception (manoeuvre relevant information, max 3 s); same scoped obligation, changed.

obligations.text: The EOR warning time shall not be extended with the time the driver's gaze is directed towards the dashboard or instrument panel.
obligations.reason: New sentence with no counterpart in o258 or other candidates; it adds a separate constraint on EOR warning timing.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 first sentence: driver deemed visually reengaged after aversion if eye gaze or head posture re-directed to a driving task relevant area (excluding dashboard and instrument panel) for sufficient duration
5.5.4.2.5.2.1 second sentence: duration at least 200 milliseconds

obligations.text: The driver shall be deemed visually reengaged following an aversion of eye gaze or head posture if either is re-directed towards any currently driving task relevant area, with the exception of the dashboard and the instrument panel, for a sufficient duration depending on the situation.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and same scoped reengagement criterion as o259; changed by removing 'engaged or' and adding the dashboard/instrument panel exception.

obligations.text: The sufficient duration for the driver to be deemed visually reengaged shall be at least 200 milliseconds.
obligations.reason: Unchanged minimum duration of 200 ms from o259 for the same reengagement assessment.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.5.2.2: manufacturer shall specify an outline of the sufficient duration depending on the situation in documentation to the Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall specify an outline of the sufficient duration depending on the situation in the documentation provided to the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Identical to o260 (same paragraph number, same actor, action and object).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.5.3 first sentence: system designed to address detection and response to multiple subsequent short aversions of eye gaze or head posture
5.5.4.2.5.3 second sentence: manufacturer documents and explains this functionality to the Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to address the detection and response to multiple subsequent short aversions of eye gaze or head posture by the driver (e.g. increased reengagement time and/or immediate issuing of an EOR).
obligations.reason: Identical to o261, same paragraph number and scope.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document and explain to the Type Approval Authority the functionality addressing detection and response to multiple subsequent short aversions of eye gaze or head posture.
obligations.reason: Identical to o261 second sentence.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6 heading 'Warning Escalation Sequence'
5.5.4.2.6 body: the escalation sequence may start at any stage, skip stages, provide simultaneous warnings, or suppress/delay warnings while another is active, depending on the safety concept

obligations.text: Depending on the safety concept of the system, the warning escalation sequence may start directly at any of the warning stages, skip any of the warning stages, provide simultaneous warnings, or suppress or delay individual warnings in case another warning is already active.
obligations.reason: Identical to o262 (same paragraph, same permission, only page layout differs).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.1 heading 'Hands On Requests'
5.5.4.2.6.1.1 first sentence: above 10 km/h HOR given latest when driver motorically disengaged more than 5 s
5.5.4.2.6.1.1 second sentence: HOR may be delayed up to 5 s if system confirms driver not visually disengaged

obligations.text: At speeds above 10 km/h a HOR shall be given latest when the driver is deemed motorically disengaged for more than 5 seconds.
obligations.reason: Identical to o264 (same paragraph, speed and time limits).

obligations.text: At speeds above 10 km/h the HOR may be delayed for a period of up to 5 seconds as long as the system can confirm that the driver is not visually disengaged.
obligations.reason: Identical permission in o264.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.1.2 first sentence: HOR escalated latest 10 s after initial HOR in event of continued disengagement
5.5.4.2.6.1.2 second sentence: escalated HOR shall contain additional acoustic and/or haptic information

obligations.text: In the event of continued disengagement, the system shall escalate the Hands On Request (HOR) at the latest 10 seconds after the initial HOR.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o265 (same paragraph number 5.5.4.2.6.1.2, identical wording, same parent Hands On Requests); only the page changed.

obligations.text: The escalated HOR shall contain additional acoustic and/or haptic information.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o265 second sentence; identical wording under same HOR escalation paragraph.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.1.3: initiation of an HOR may be withheld per paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5

obligations.text: The initiation of an HOR may be withheld in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5.
obligations.reason: Same permission as old o266 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same parent HOR clause).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.1.4: system designed to avoid misuse (e.g. nudging steering wheel in response to HOR without becoming motorically engaged)

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to avoid misuse (e.g., nudging the steering wheel in response to an HOR without becoming, as requested by the system, motorically engaged).
obligations.reason: Same design obligation as old o267 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same HOR scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.2 heading 'Eyes On Requests'
5.5.4.2.6.2.1: at speeds above 10 km/h an EOR given latest when driver visually disengaged for 5 s

obligations.text: At speeds above 10 km/h, an Eyes On Request (EOR) shall be given at the latest when the driver is deemed visually disengaged for 5 seconds.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o269 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same EOR scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.2.2: after an EOR, if driver visually reengaged per 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 and again visually disengaged for at least 1 s within following 2 s, EOR immediately

obligations.text: Following an EOR, if the driver has been deemed visually reengaged according to paragraph 5.5.4.2.5.2.1 and subsequently starts to be visually disengaged again for at least 1 second within the following 2 seconds, an EOR shall be given immediately.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old o270 (same paragraph number, same wording apart from punctuation in the cross-reference, same re-disengagement EOR scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.2.3 first sentence: escalate EOR at latest 3 s after initial EOR with increased intensity upon continued visual disengagement
5.5.4.2.6.2.3 second sentence: escalated EOR shall always contain acoustic and/or haptic information

obligations.text: In the event of continued visual disengagement, the system shall escalate the EOR at the latest 3 seconds after the initial EOR, according to the warning strategy, with increased intensity.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o271 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same parent EOR context); no substantive change.

obligations.text: The escalated EOR (issued upon continued visual disengagement) shall always contain acoustic and/or haptic information.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as the second sentence of old clause o271 under the same Eyes On Requests parent; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.3 heading 'Direct Control Alerts'
5.5.4.2.6.3.1: DCA presented to driver at latest 5 s following EOR escalation

obligations.text: At the latest 5 seconds following an escalation of the EOR, a DCA (Direct Control Alert) shall be presented to the driver.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o273 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same Direct Control Alerts parent); unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.4 heading 'Transition to Driver Unavailability Response'
5.5.4.2.6.4.1: initiate driver unavailability response at latest 10 s after first escalated request or DCA if driver continues to be disengaged

obligations.text: If the system determines the driver to continue to be disengaged following a warning escalation, the system shall initiate a driver unavailability response at the latest 10 seconds after the first escalated request or DCA.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o275 (same paragraph, identical wording, same Transition to Driver Unavailability Response parent); unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Intro sentence 1: system may withhold HORs on Highway or Highway-like road at speed up to 130 km/h (permission)
Intro sentence 2: manufacturer shall describe boundary conditions for withholding HORs in documentation per 5.3.5.2 / section 9
Intro sentence 3: when capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads, system shall aim to avoid frequent fluctuations between able and not able to withhold
(a)(i)/(ii): verify road ahead characteristics for at least 500 m or at least 30 s before initiating withholding
(a) alternative strategies: equivalent duration strategies documented and demonstrated to TAA
(b): manufacturer shall demonstrate safe operation with cyclists by collision avoidance per Annex 4 4.2.5.2.16 with Annex 3 Appendix 4 robustness criteria
(c): HOR aim to be given at least 7 s before driver-controlled manoeuvre at end of highway-like road
Closing sentence: subparagraphs apply while in this mode on highway or highway-like road
coverage.exclusion_reason: Lead-in applicability statement for following subparagraphs; no separate obligation.

obligations.text: The system may withhold HORs when the vehicle is located on a "Highway" or a "Highway-like" road and is operated at a speed up to 130 km/h.
obligations.reason: Replaces the permission in old o276 (same paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.5, Withholding of HORs) extending scope from "Highway" only to "Highway" or "Highway-like" roads.

obligations.text: As outlined in paragraph 5.3.5.2., the manufacturer shall describe in detail, as part of the documentation required for section 9, the boundary conditions under which HORs can be withheld.
obligations.reason: Same documentation obligation as in old o276, same paragraph and wording; unchanged.

obligations.text: When the system is capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads, it shall aim to avoid frequent fluctuations between being able and not able to withhold HORs (e.g., not operating on discontinuous sections of highway-like roads).
obligations.reason: Highway-like road scope is new; old o276 covered only Highway and had no fluctuation-avoidance requirement.

obligations.text: When capable of withholding HORs on highway-like roads, the system shall aim to ensure a reasonable duration of being able to withhold HORs by verifying one or more of the following before initiating withholding: (i) the road ahead is deemed to have the necessary characteristics (per paragraph 2.28.1.) for at least 500 m, or (ii) for at least 30 seconds at the vehicle's current speed.
obligations.reason: No equivalent road-ahead duration verification in old o276 or other candidates.

obligations.text: As an alternative to the 500 m / 30 s road-ahead verification, the system may implement other strategies reasonably expected to result in at least an equivalent duration; the manufacturer shall document such strategies and demonstrate them to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: New alternative-strategy provision with documentation and demonstration duty; not in old clauses.

obligations.text: For HOR withholding, the manufacturer shall demonstrate the system's ability to safely operate in the presence of cyclists, by avoidance of a collision with a longitudinally travelling cyclist ahead in lane as outlined in Annex 4, paragraph 4.2.5.2.16., taking into account the robustness criteria in Appendix 4 of Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Cyclist collision-avoidance demonstration is not in old o276 or other candidates.

obligations.text: When the end of a highway-like road is expected to require a manoeuvre controlled by the driver, an HOR shall aim to be given at least 7 seconds before the necessary manoeuvre needs to start.
obligations.reason: New timing requirement for highway-like road ends; absent from old o276.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.1 first sentence: HOR at latest 5 s before detected upcoming boundary condition
5.5.4.2.6.5.1 second sentence: DCA for situations not detected 5 s in advance unless lateral assistance continues after motoric reengagement
5.5.4.2.6.5.1 third sentence: HOR upon detection where DCA is not issued
5.5.4.2.6.5.1 final paragraph: manufacturer demonstrates controllability to TAA

obligations.text: In case of a detected upcoming boundary condition which requires an HOR, the system shall give the HOR at the latest 5 seconds in advance of reaching the boundary condition(s).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o277 (identical paragraph number 5.5.4.2.6.5.1, identical text); paragraph existed before, only page changed.

obligations.text: For situations in which an upcoming boundary condition requiring an HOR is not detected 5 seconds in advance, the system shall issue a DCA unless lateral assistance will still be provided after the driver is motorically reengaged.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o277 second sentence; same paragraph, unchanged wording and scope.

obligations.text: Where a DCA is not issued for a situation not detected 5 seconds in advance, the system shall issue an HOR upon detection of the upcoming boundary condition(s).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o277 third sentence; unchanged.

obligations.text: In addition to the requirements of paragraph 5.3.6., for situations not detected 5 seconds in advance, the vehicle manufacturer shall demonstrate the controllability of such situations to the Type Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety concept.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old o277 last paragraph; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.2 whole sentence: HOR or DCA upon reaching system boundaries due to driver acceleration override

obligations.text: The system shall issue an HOR or DCA as appropriate upon reaching the system boundaries due to a driver override of the longitudinal control by acceleration.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o278 (same paragraph number and scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.3 whole sentence: driver able to override accelerator input suppression

obligations.text: If the system has the ability to suppress accelerator input in order to avoid exceeding the system boundaries, the driver shall be able to override this.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o279 (same paragraph and scope).

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.4 first sentence and table: latest EOR timing by speed (130 km/h 3.5 s; 10-60 km/h 5.0 s)
5.5.4.2.6.5.4 last sentence: linear interpolation between 60 and 130 km/h

obligations.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.4.2.6.2.1., an EOR shall be given at the latest when the driver has been deemed visually disengaged for the relevant time period: 3.5 s at 130 km/h; 5.0 s at 10 km/h to 60 km/h.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o280 (same paragraph and table).

obligations.text: For vehicle speeds between 60 km/h and 130 km/h, a linear interpolation shall be used to calculate the corresponding latest EOR timing.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o280 last sentence.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.5 first sentence: system designed to determine no deviation in eye gaze/head position for significant time
5.5.4.2.6.5.5 second sentence: EOR issued in this case
5.5.4.2.6.5.5 third sentence: strategies documented and explained to TAA

obligations.text: The system shall be designed to determine when there has been no deviation in eye gaze (or movement of head position when this is being used to determine visual engagement) for a significant period of time.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o281 (same paragraph and scope).

obligations.text: An EOR shall be issued when there has been no deviation in eye gaze (or head position movement when used to determine visual engagement) for a significant period of time.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o281 second sentence.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document and explain to the Type Approval Authority the strategies for determining no deviation in eye gaze/head position.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o281 third sentence.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.6 first sentence: inform driver whether HORs are withheld, clearly distinguishable
5.5.4.2.6.5.6 second sentence: information not to promote removing hands (steering wheel without hands indication permitted)

obligations.text: The system shall inform the driver whether HORs are currently being withheld or not in a clearly distinguishable way.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o282 (same paragraph and scope).

obligations.text: The information on whether HORs are withheld shall be designed to not actively promote that the driver should remove their hands from the steering control (an indication of a steering wheel without hands is not considered to violate this requirement).
obligations.reason: Identical to old o282 second sentence.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.4.2.6.5.7 heading: Additional monitoring requirements for systems capable of system-initiated manoeuvres whilst withholding HORs
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; imposes no obligation itself. Requirements are in subparagraphs 5.5.4.2.6.5.7.1 to .3.
