coverage.source_unit: 3. General principles (heading)
3.1. Test conditions (heading)
3.1.1 first sentence: tests performed under conditions allowing activation of system or features
3.1.1 second sentence: manufacturer demonstrates safe control for untested conditions within system boundaries via Annex 3 audit

obligations.text: Tests shall be performed under conditions (e.g. environmental, road geometry) that allow the activation of the system or specific features thereof.
obligations.reason: Same scoped test-condition requirement as old o602 (Annex 4 / 3.1.1), identical wording and scope, same paragraph number.

obligations.text: For conditions not tested that may occur within the defined system boundaries of the vehicle, the manufacturer shall demonstrate, as part of the audit described in Annex 3, to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that the vehicle is safely controlled.
obligations.reason: Same manufacturer demonstration obligation as old o602 (Annex 4 / 3.1.1), unchanged scope and audit reference.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.2 first sentence: if system modifications are required for testing, ensure no effect on test results
3.1.2 second sentence: modifications documented and annexed to test report
3.1.2 third sentence: description and evidence of influence (if any) documented and annexed to test report

obligations.text: If system modifications are required in order to allow testing (e.g. road type assessment criteria), it shall be ensured that these modifications do not have an effect on the test results.
obligations.reason: Same as old o603 (Annex 4 / 3.1.2), identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: Where system modifications are made to allow testing, these modifications shall be documented and annexed to the test report.
obligations.reason: Same as old o603 (Annex 4 / 3.1.2), identical documentation obligation.

obligations.text: The description and the evidence of influence (if any) of the testing-related system modifications shall be documented and annexed to the test report.
obligations.reason: Same as old o603 (Annex 4 / 3.1.2), identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.3 first paragraph: permission to artificially induce errors and bring vehicle to limits of operating range to test failure, self-testing and initialisation
3.1.3 second paragraph: verify system condition matches intended testing purpose

obligations.text: In order to test the requirements for failure of functions, self-testing and initialisation of the system, errors may be artificially induced and the vehicle may be artificially brought into situations where it reaches the limits of the defined operating range (e.g., environmental conditions).
obligations.reason: Same permission as old o604 (Annex 4 / 3.1.3), identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: It shall be verified that the condition of the system is according to the intended testing purpose (e.g. in a fault-free condition or with the specific faults to be tested).
obligations.reason: Same verification requirement as old o604 (Annex 4 / 3.1.3), identical wording.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.4 test surface adhesion requirement

obligations.text: The test surface shall afford at least the adhesion required by the scenario in order to achieve the expected test result.
obligations.reason: Same as old o605 (Annex 4 / 3.1.4), identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5. Test Targets (heading only)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; imposes no obligation of its own.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.1 first sentence: vehicle detection test target is a series production Category M or N vehicle or an ISO 19206-3 soft target
3.1.5.1 second sentence: reference point for vehicle location

obligations.text: The target used for vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production vehicle of Category M or N, or alternatively a "soft target" representative of a vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the sensor equipment of the system under test, according to ISO 19206-3.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o607 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.1): same paragraph number, same target type, same ISO 19206-3 alternative. Only the page changed.

obligations.text: For vehicle detection tests, the reference point for the location of the vehicle shall be the most rearward point on the centreline of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as the second sentence of o607 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.1): same reference point definition for the vehicle target. Wording unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.2 first sentence: Powered-Two-wheeler test target is an ISO 19206-5 test device or a type approved series production L3 motorcycle
3.1.5.2 second sentence: reference point for motorcycle location

obligations.text: The target used for Powered-Two-wheeler tests shall be a test device according to ISO 19206-5 or a type approved high volume series production motorcycle of Category L3.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o608 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.2): same PTW target and alternatives. Only the page changed.

obligations.text: For Powered-Two-wheeler tests, the reference point for the location of the motorcycle shall be the most backward point on the centreline of the motorcycle.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as the second sentence of o608 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.2): same motorcycle reference point. Wording unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.3 sentence: pedestrian detection test target is an articulated soft target per ISO 19206-2, representative of human attributes

obligations.text: The target used for pedestrian detection tests shall be an "articulated soft target" representative of the human attributes applicable to the sensor equipment of the system under test, according to ISO 19206-2.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o609 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.3): same pedestrian target and ISO 19206-2 requirement. Wording unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.4 first sentence: bicycle detection test target is an ISO 19206-4 device
3.1.5.4 second sentence: reference point for bicycle location

obligations.text: The target used for bicycle detection tests shall be a device according to ISO 19206-4.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o610 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.4): same bicycle target and ISO 19206-4 requirement. Wording unchanged.

obligations.text: For bicycle detection tests, the reference point for the location of the bicycle shall be the most forward point on the centreline of the bicycle.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as the second sentence of o610 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.4): same bicycle reference point. Wording unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.5 first sentence: permission to use driverless robotised vehicles or state-of-the-art test tools in place of reference targets
3.1.5.5 second sentence: replacement test tools must have comparable characteristics and be agreed between Type Approval Authority and manufacturer

obligations.text: As an alternative to reference targets, driverless robotised vehicles or state-of-the-art test tools (e.g. soft targets, mobile platforms) may be used to carry out the tests, replacing real vehicles and other road users that could reasonably be encountered within the system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same scoped permission as the first sentence of o611 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.5): same alternative test tools and scope. Wording unchanged.

obligations.text: It shall be ensured that test tools replacing the reference targets have comparable characteristics to the vehicle or road user they represent, and are in agreement between the Type Approval Authority and the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as the second sentence of o611 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.5): same comparability and agreement condition. Wording unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.5.6 – details enabling specific identification and reproduction of targets shall be recorded in vehicle type approval documentation

obligations.text: Details that enable the test target(s) to be specifically identified and reproduced shall be recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o612 (Annex 4 / 3.1.5.6, Test Targets); identical wording and parent context, only renumbered page.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.6 heading 'Test parameter variation'
3.1.6.1 first sentence – manufacturer shall declare system boundaries to the Type Approval Authority
3.1.6.1 second sentence – Type Approval Authority shall define different combinations of test parameters

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall declare the system boundaries to the Type Approval Authority (for test parameter variation).
obligations.reason: Same actor/action/scope as o614 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.1), identical text under the same Test parameter variation parent.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall define different combinations of test parameters (e.g., present speed of the vehicle under test, type and offset of the target, curvature of lane).
obligations.reason: Same obligation as o614 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.1), unchanged wording and context.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.6.2 sentence 1 – base tests shall be carried out at least 2 times to confirm consistency
3.1.6.2 sentence 2 – repeat test once if one of two runs fails
3.1.6.2 sentence 3 – pass criterion: required performance met in two runs and manufacturer evidence per Annex 3 Appendix 4
3.1.6.2 sentence 4 – TAA may require additional test runs

obligations.text: To confirm consistency of the system, base tests shall be carried out at least 2 times.
obligations.reason: Same as o615 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.2); identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: If one of the two base test runs fails to meet the required performance, the test shall be repeated once.
obligations.reason: Same as o615 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.2); unchanged.

obligations.text: A base test shall be accounted as passed if the required performance is met in two test runs and the manufacturer has provided sufficient evidence according to Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same as o615 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.2); unchanged pass criterion.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority may choose to require additional test runs to confirm the declaration thresholds outlined in Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o615 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.2); unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.6.3 sentence 1 – system shall not unreasonably switch control strategy when conditions deviate from base test; verified by extended testing
3.1.6.3 sentence 3 – each parameter in extended tests shall be varied; variations may be grouped into a single test design
3.1.6.3 sentence 4 – TAA may request additional documentation on untested parameter variations

obligations.text: When conditions deviate from those specified for the base test, the system shall not unreasonably switch its control strategy; this shall be verified by the extended testing.
obligations.reason: Same as o616 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.3); identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: Each parameter as outlined in the extended tests shall be varied, where variations can be grouped into a single test design.
obligations.reason: Same as o616 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.3); unchanged.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority may request additional documentation evidencing the system's performance under parameter variations not tested.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o616 (Annex 4 / 3.1.6.3); unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 3.1.7 heading 'Public road verification'
3.1.7.1 first sentence: TAA shall conduct or witness assessment of system in fault-free condition in traffic in at least one country (where applicable to feature type)
3.1.7.1 second sentence: purpose statement
coverage.exclusion_reason: Statement of purpose; not a separate obligation

obligations.text: Where applicable to the type of feature of the system, the Type Approval Authority shall conduct, or shall witness, an assessment of the system in a fault-free condition, in the presence of traffic, in at least one country of operation, to assess the behaviour of the system in its operating environment.
obligations.reason: Identical scoped public road verification obligation at same paragraph number as o618 (Annex 4 / 3.1.7.1), same actor, action, scope; only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 4. Test procedures (heading)
4.1 sentence 1: compliance shall be demonstrated by physical test for the following paragraphs
4.1 sentence 2: variations of the same test may be demonstrated by other means in agreement with TAA

obligations.text: Compliance with the requirements of this UN Regulation shall be demonstrated by physical test for the paragraphs referenced in the following test scenarios.
obligations.reason: Same as o620 (Annex 4 / 4.1), unchanged wording and scope.

obligations.text: Variations of the same test (e.g. reaching different boundary conditions) may be demonstrated by other means (e.g. part of the audit described in Annex 3 or virtual testing) in agreement with the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o620 (Annex 4 / 4.1), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 4.1.1 sentence 1: requirements/aspects to be tested in physical tests are in table 1; chosen based on system boundaries
4.1.1 scenarios shall be created and described in agreement with TAA
4.1.1 each requirement or aspect assessed at least through track testing or public road verification
4.1.1 a given scenario may be used to assess different requirements/aspects
4.1.1 test scenarios shall be created depending on preconditions for activation and system boundaries
Table A4/1 mapping of requirements to physical test scenarios/audit, with agreed scenarios for starred items

obligations.text: Requirements and system aspects listed in Table A4/1 shall be tested during the physical tests; the relevant requirements or system aspects shall be chosen based on the system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Matches o621 (Annex 4 / 4.1.1), same scope and wording.

obligations.text: Scenarios with the aim of testing a given requirement or aspect shall be created and described in agreement with the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same sentence in o621 (4.1.1).

obligations.text: Each requirement or aspect shall be assessed at least through track testing or public road verification.
obligations.reason: Same sentence in o621 (4.1.1).

obligations.text: A given scenario may be used to assess different requirements / aspects of the system. Test scenarios shall be created depending on the system preconditions for activation and system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same permission and scenario creation condition in o621 (4.1.1).

obligations.text: Test scenarios shall be created depending on the system preconditions for activation and system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Same sentence in o621 (4.1.1).

obligations.text: Table A4/1 assigns each requirement or system aspect to physical test scenarios or audit (Annex 3 / 4.1.1, 4.2.x, 4.3.x); for items marked *, scenarios and test procedures shall be agreed between the manufacturer and the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Table content matches o621 Table A4/1 (same rows and references).

coverage.source_unit: 4.2 heading
4.2.1 test scenarios shall be selected depending on preconditions for activation and system boundaries

obligations.text: Test scenarios shall be selected depending on the system's preconditions for activation and system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Identical to o623 (Annex 4 / 4.2.1), same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.2 first sentence: tests may be performed on a test track or, where possible and without safety risk, on public roads
4.2.2 second sentence: scenarios that may cause danger shall be aimed to be tested on a test track

obligations.text: The tests can be performed either on a test track or, where possible and without any safety risk to the vehicle occupants and other road users, on public roads.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number 4.2.2 with identical text to old o624, in the same Annex 4 / 4.2 context.

obligations.text: Test scenarios that may cause danger to other road users and the test personnel (e.g. AEB equivalent performance, driver unavailability response, high lateral accelerations) shall be aimed to be tested on a test track.
obligations.reason: Identical to the second sentence of old o624 with the same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.2.1 intro: tests shall be performed so the outcome is not affected by driver settings, driver input or other influences unrelated to the manoeuvre
(a)(i) following distance set to default distance if reset upon first activation after powertrain initiation; (ii) otherwise closest driver adjustable distance
(b) set speed set to the speed indicated in the test or declared by the manufacturer per Annex 3 Appendix 4
(c) system must be in active mode before the lower of 10 s TTC or 250 m relative longitudinal distance
(d) no corrective driver input to the steering control
Final sentence: manufacturer shall declare any other relevant conditions for correct execution of each test

obligations.text: Tests shall be performed so that the outcome is not affected by driver settings, driver input or any other influences not related to the manoeuvre under test.
obligations.reason: Identical to the intro of old o625 (same number, same context).

obligations.text: During tests, the system's longitudinal control following distance shall be set to the default distance if the distance is reset to a specific value upon first activation after powertrain initiation, or to the closest driver adjustable following distance if it is not reset to a default value.
obligations.reason: Same as item (a) of old o625.

obligations.text: During tests, the system's longitudinal control set speed shall be set to the speed indicated in the test or the speed declared by the manufacturer according to Annex 3 Appendix 4.
obligations.reason: Same as item (b) of old o625.

obligations.text: During tests, the system must be in 'active' mode before the lower of 10 s TTC or 250 m relative longitudinal distance.
obligations.reason: Same as item (c) of old o625.

obligations.text: During tests there shall be no corrective driver input to the steering control.
obligations.reason: Same as item (d) of old o625.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall declare any other relevant conditions to be met for correct execution of each test.
obligations.reason: Same as final sentence of old o625.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.2.2: for systems with non-repeatable outcomes under identical initial conditions, manufacturer shall explain the deviation to the Type Approval Authority and agree on parameterization ranges

obligations.text: For systems where identical initial conditions (e.g. path or positioning) in a given scenario may not always result in a repeatable outcome (e.g. non-rule-based algorithms), the manufacturer shall explain this deviation to and agree with the Type Approval Authority on the ranges of test parameterization that do not modify the objective of the test scenario and diverge from other requirements of this regulation.
obligations.reason: New paragraph. Candidates o620, o662 and o486 cover different scopes (variations by other means, extended testing, simulation) and give no evidence of continuity.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.3: tests must not endanger personnel; significant vehicle damage must be avoided where other means of validation are available

obligations.text: Tests must not be carried out in such a way as to endanger the personnel involved, and significant damage of the vehicle under test must be avoided where other means of validation are available.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o626, same number and context.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.4 heading: Lane Markings and Lane Geometry
4.2.4.1 main: where base tests are on a curved section, geometry shall fulfil the table criteria (S-bend; clothoid parameters, radii, lengths)
4.2.4.1 final sentence: at manufacturer request and with TAA agreement, tests may be conducted on a road of different curvature if intention/severity not lowered

obligations.text: Where base tests are required to be performed on a curved section of road, the geometry shall fulfil the criteria in the table (S-bend means both turns in the listed order; curved section means the 2nd turn). First turn (any direction): clothoid parameter 153.7 with length 30.0 m; radius 787 m with length 57.1 m; clothoid parameter 105.0 with length 14.0 m. Second turn (opposite direction to the 1st): clothoid parameter 98.6 with length 26 m; radius 374 m with length 5.1 m; clothoid parameter 120.8 with length 39 m.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o628 (same number, same context, same table values).

obligations.text: At the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Type Approval Authority, tests may be conducted on a road of different curvature, provided this does not change the intention or lower the severity of the test.
obligations.reason: Identical to the final sentence of old o628.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5 – Type Approval Authority shall conduct or witness at least the following tests to assess system behaviour based on declared operating domains

obligations.text: At the time of type approval, the Type Approval Authority shall conduct or shall witness at least the following tests to assess the behaviour of the system based on the declared operating domains.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o629 (Annex 4 / 4.2.5): identical actor (Type Approval Authority), action (conduct or witness tests at type approval), and scope (declared operating domains); only renumbered page.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1 – heading 'Test scenarios for different DCAS Features'
4.2.5.1.1 – heading 'Positioning in the lane of travel'
4.2.5.1.1.1 Base Test – test shall confirm declared lane positioning capabilities

obligations.text: Base Test for positioning in the lane of travel: the test shall confirm the positioning in the lane of travel capabilities declared by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o632 (4.2.5.1.1.1) under the same lane-positioning parent; wording and scope unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.1.1.1 para 1 – VUT speed shall remain in manufacturer-declared range (9.1.1, 9.1.2)
4.2.5.1.1.1.1 para 2 – test carried out for each declared speed range separately or within contiguous ranges with identical declared max lateral acceleration
4.2.5.1.1.1.1 para 3 – VUT driven hands-off at constant speed on curved track with lane markings both sides
4.2.5.1.1.1.1 para 4 – lateral acceleration 80-90 per cent of declared maximum

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test at 80-90 per cent of declared maximum lateral acceleration, the VUT speed shall remain in the range declared by the manufacturer in paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. of this UN Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same scoped step as old o633 (4.2.5.1.1.1.1); unchanged wording and scope.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test at 80-90 per cent of declared maximum lateral acceleration, the test shall be carried out for each speed range declared by the manufacturer in paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. separately, or within contiguous speed ranges where the declared maximum lateral acceleration is identical.
obligations.reason: Same scoped requirement as old o633; unchanged.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test at 80-90 per cent of declared maximum lateral acceleration, the VUT shall be driven without any force applied by the driver on the steering control (e.g. hands removed) at constant speed on a curved track with lane markings at each side.
obligations.reason: Same scoped test procedure step as old o633; unchanged.

obligations.text: The lateral acceleration necessary to follow the curve shall be between 80 and 90 per cent of the maximum lateral acceleration declared by the manufacturer in Annex 3 Appendix 4 of this UN Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same scoped test target as old o633; unchanged values.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.1.1.2 para 1 – VUT speed shall remain in declared range
4.2.5.1.1.1.2 para 2 – test for each declared speed range separately or contiguous ranges with identical max lateral acceleration
4.2.5.1.1.1.2 para 3 – VUT driven hands-off at constant speed on curved track with lane markings
4.2.5.1.1.1.2 para 4 – TAA defines test speed and radius provoking acceleration higher than declared max + 0.3 m/s2

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test exceeding declared maximum lateral acceleration, the VUT speed shall remain in the range declared by the manufacturer in paragraphs 9.1.1. and 9.1.2. of this UN Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same scoped step as old o634 (4.2.5.1.1.1.2); unchanged.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test exceeding declared maximum lateral acceleration, the test shall be carried out for each declared speed range separately, or within contiguous speed ranges where the declared maximum lateral acceleration is identical.
obligations.reason: Same scoped requirement as old o634; unchanged.

obligations.text: In the lane positioning test exceeding declared maximum lateral acceleration, the VUT shall be driven without any force applied by the driver on the steering control (e.g. hands removed) at constant speed on a curved track with lane markings at each side.
obligations.reason: Same scoped procedure step as old o634; unchanged.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall define a test speed and a radius which would provoke a higher acceleration than the declared maximum lateral acceleration + 0.3 m/s2 (e.g. by travelling at higher speed through a curve of given radius).
obligations.reason: Old o634 had identical text for this step; the new text is treated as the same scoped obligation, with 'declared maximum lateral acceleration + 0.3 m/s2' wording unchanged. Marked existing-equivalent.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.1.1.3 – alternative-means permission (manufacturer request, TAA agreement, track unavailable)
4.2.5.1.1.1.3 – proviso: at least one physical test at overall declared maximum lateral acceleration for each of 4.2.5.1.1.1.1 and 4.2.5.1.1.1.2

obligations.text: At the manufacturer's request and with Type Approval Authority agreement, meeting the objectives of paragraphs 5.3.7.1.1., 5.3.7.1.2. or 6.1.1., as applicable, across all speed ranges where the declared maximum lateral acceleration differs may be demonstrated through alternative means when test tracks with an appropriate radius for the lateral acceleration conditions of 4.2.5.1.1.1.1. or 4.2.5.1.1.1.2. are not available.
obligations.reason: Same scoped permission as old o635 (same paragraph number, identical wording, same parent test context); only pagination differs.

obligations.text: When alternative means are used because tracks with an appropriate radius are not available, at least one physical test as outlined in 4.2.5.1.1.1.1. and 4.2.5.1.1.1.2. shall be performed at the overall declared maximum lateral acceleration for each of those paragraphs.
obligations.reason: Same proviso as in old o635 (same paragraph, identical wording and scope).

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.1.2 Extended Testing – test shall demonstrate system stays in ego lane with stable motion across speed range and curvatures up to declared max lateral acceleration

obligations.text: Extended Testing: the test shall demonstrate that the system does not leave its lane and maintains a stable motion inside its ego lane across the speed range and different curvatures within its system boundaries up to the maximum lateral acceleration declared by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o636 (same paragraph number, same text and scope).

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.1.2.1 (a) sufficient length for assessment
4.2.5.1.1.2.1 (b) different curvatures incl. S-bend and initial speeds, one requiring exceeding declared max lateral acceleration
4.2.5.1.1.2.1 (c) different types of lane boundaries

obligations.text: For the positioning-in-lane Extended Testing, the test shall be executed at least with sufficient length to allow for an assessment of positioning in the lane of travel behaviour.
obligations.reason: Matches old o637 item (a): same paragraph, identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: For the positioning-in-lane Extended Testing, the test shall be executed at least for different road curvatures, including an S-bend with the parameters according to paragraph 4.2.4.1. or equivalent, and different initial speeds, at least one of which would require the vehicle to exceed the maximum lateral acceleration declared by the manufacturer in order to remain in the lane at this speed.
obligations.reason: Matches old o637 item (b): same paragraph, identical wording and scope.

obligations.text: For the positioning-in-lane Extended Testing, the test shall be executed at least with different types of lane boundaries (e.g. markings, road edges, only one lane marking) as applicable to the system.
obligations.reason: Matches old o637 item (c): same paragraph, identical wording and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.2 Driver-initiated Lane changes – heading only
4.2.5.1.2.1 Base Test – test shall confirm declared driver-initiated lane changing capabilities

obligations.text: Base Test: the test shall confirm the driver-initiated lane changing capabilities of the system declared by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o639 (same paragraph number, text and driver-initiated scope).

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.2.1.1 VUT performs full lane change (e.g. 3.5 m) after driver initiated LCP

obligations.text: In the driver-initiated lane change Base Test, the VUT shall perform a full lane change (e.g., 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane after the driver initiated the LCP.
obligations.reason: Identical to old o640 (same paragraph, driver-initiated LCP scope); not the system-initiated o645.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.2.2 intro: Extended Testing - test shall assess system's ability to assist driver in changing lanes safely within boundary conditions/declared features
(a) On roads without physical separation
(b) On roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited
(c) Where the lane change cannot be executed immediately after initiation by the driver
(d) Presence of a lead vehicle

obligations.text: In the extended testing of driver-initiated lane changes, the test shall assess the system's ability to assist the driver, within its boundary conditions/manufacturer's declared system features, in changing lanes safely.
obligations.reason: Same scoped driver-initiated extended test obligation relocated to new page; identical to o641 under same parent 4.2.5.1.2.

obligations.text: In the driver-initiated lane change extended testing, the test shall assess safe lane-change assistance on roads without physical separation.
obligations.reason: Same case as o641(a), same scope.

obligations.text: In the driver-initiated lane change extended testing, the test shall assess safe lane-change assistance on roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited.
obligations.reason: Same case as o641(b), same scope.

obligations.text: In the driver-initiated lane change extended testing, the test shall assess safe lane-change assistance where the lane change cannot be executed immediately after its initiation by the driver.
obligations.reason: Same case as o641(c), same scope.

obligations.text: In the driver-initiated lane change extended testing, the test shall assess safe lane-change assistance in the presence of a lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same case as o641(d), same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.2.2.1 intro: test shall be executed at least (scope: driver-initiated extended test)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Shared introductory condition; applied to each case.

coverage.source_unit: (a) road with oncoming or overtaking traffic in target lane
(b) different road users approaching from rear
(c) vehicle beside in adjacent lane preventing lane change
(d) system reacts to another vehicle starting to change into same space in target lane

obligations.text: The driver-initiated lane change extended test shall be executed at least on a road with oncoming or overtaking traffic in the target lane.
obligations.reason: Same as o642(a), same parent 4.2.5.1.2.2; not o648 which is system-initiated scope.

obligations.text: The driver-initiated lane change extended test shall be executed at least with different road users approaching from the rear.
obligations.reason: Same as o642(b).

obligations.text: The driver-initiated lane change extended test shall be executed at least with a vehicle driving beside in the adjacent lane preventing a lane change.
obligations.reason: Same as o642(c).

obligations.text: The driver-initiated lane change extended test shall be executed at least in a scenario where the system reacts to another vehicle that starts changing into the same space within the target lane, to avoid a potential risk of collision.
obligations.reason: Same as o642(d).

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.3 heading: Driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes
4.2.5.1.3.1 Base Test: test shall confirm system-initiated lane changing capabilities declared by manufacturer

obligations.text: The base test for driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes shall confirm the system-initiated lane changing capabilities declared by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Identical to o644 under same parent 4.2.5.1.3; relocated page only.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.3.1.1 VUT shall perform full lane change (e.g., 3.5 m) after system has initiated the LCP

obligations.text: In the base test for system-initiated lane changes, the VUT shall perform a full lane change (e.g., 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane after the system has initiated the LCP.
obligations.reason: Identical to o645 under same parent 4.2.5.1.3.1.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.3.1.2 VUT and lead vehicle travel straight, same direction, at least 2 s before functional part, centreline offset not more than 1 m

obligations.text: In the base test for system-initiated lane changes, the VUT and the lead vehicle shall travel in a straight line, in the same direction, for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test with a VUT to lead vehicle centreline offset of not more than 1 m.
obligations.reason: Identical to o646 under same parent 4.2.5.1.3.1.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.3.2 Extended Testing: test shall demonstrate system can assist driver in changing lanes safely, with (a) other speed differences between lead vehicle and VUT; (b) roads without physical separation; and/or (c) roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited

obligations.text: The extended test for driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes shall demonstrate that the system is able to assist the driver in changing lanes safely: (a) with other speed differences between the lead vehicle and the VUT; (b) on roads without physical separation; and/or (c) on roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited.
obligations.reason: Relocated/renumbered with the same paragraph number; identical wording and same parent scope (4.2.5.1.3 lane changes) as o647.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.1.3.2.1 test executed at least: (a) road with oncoming or overtaking traffic in target lane; (b) different road users approaching from rear; (c) vehicle beside in adjacent lane preventing lane change; (d) system reacts to another vehicle starting to change into same space in target lane

obligations.text: For the extended lane-change test (driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes), the test shall be executed at least: (a) on a road with oncoming or overtaking traffic in the target lane; (b) with different road users approaching from the rear; (c) with a vehicle driving beside in the adjacent lane preventing a lane change; (d) in a scenario where the system reacts to another vehicle that starts changing into the same space within the target lane, to avoid a potential risk of collision.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number and identical wording under the same parent 4.2.5.1.3.2 as o648; not the driver-initiated o642 scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2 Heading: Ability to respond to another road user corresponding to the declared operating domains
4.2.5.2.1 Heading: Stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road
4.2.5.2.1.1 Base Test: test shall confirm declared response capability for stationary vehicle ahead on straight road

obligations.text: Base Test: The test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number, identical wording and same stationary-vehicle-straight-road scope as o651.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.1.1.1 VUT shall approach stationary target in straight line for at least 2 s before functional part with centreline offset not more than 0.5 m

obligations.reason: Identical wording to o680 but under the separate new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17; separate scoped test target, not shown to be a renumbering.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.17.2.1 intro and item (a): stationary vehicle target of different type or category, incl. cyclist and pedestrian if system designed for non-highway roads
item (b): cut-out at less than 3 s TTC of lead vehicle
item (c): different speeds of VUT and lead vehicle
item (d): different lateral acceleration of lead vehicle
item (e): impassable objects

obligations.text: The extended cut-out test with an interfering vehicle shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle target of a different type or category, including cyclist and pedestrian if the system is designed to drive in non-highway roads.
obligations.reason: Scoped to the new interfering-vehicle extended test; differs from o681 (adds cyclist/pedestrian) and applies to a separate scenario.

obligations.text: The extended cut-out test with an interfering vehicle shall be executed at least with the cut-out occurring at less than 3 seconds TTC of the lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: Repeated condition under the new interfering-vehicle scenario; separate scoped obligation.

obligations.text: The extended cut-out test with an interfering vehicle shall be executed at least with different speeds of the VUT and lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: Repeated condition under the new scenario; separate scoped obligation.

obligations.text: The extended cut-out test with an interfering vehicle shall be executed at least with different lateral acceleration of the lead vehicle.
obligations.reason: Repeated condition under the new scenario; separate scoped obligation.

obligations.text: The extended cut-out test with an interfering vehicle shall be executed at least with impassable objects.
obligations.reason: Newly added test condition with no old counterpart.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.18 heading: Pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; introduces a test scenario and contains no independent obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.18.1 Base Test: test shall confirm declared response capability for crossing pedestrian target while other vehicle obstructs lane and perception

obligations.text: Base Test for pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a crossing pedestrian target, while another vehicle obstructs the lane of travel and the perception of the pedestrian target.
obligations.reason: New scenario (obstructed lane and perception during drive around). Candidate o702 covers a plain crossing pedestrian without obstruction or drive around; it is not the same scoped obligation.

coverage.source_unit: Static target placed in front of VUT with 50% overlap towards road edge
VUT shall travel at least 30 km/h toward static target with system-initiated manoeuvring activated
VUT shall avoid collision with target if performing drive around manoeuvre

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test, a static target shall be placed in front of the VUT with 50% overlap towards the edge of the road.
obligations.reason: Setup is scoped to the new 4.2.5.2.18 scenario. Candidate o740 is a different scenario (oncoming vehicle, synchronized timing), so equivalence is not established.

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test, the VUT shall travel at least 30 km/h toward the static target with system-initiated manoeuvring activated.
obligations.reason: Speed and activation condition apply to the new scenario; the old o740/o741 context differs (adjacent-lane moving vehicle target).

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test, the VUT shall avoid collision with the target if performing a drive around manoeuvre.
obligations.reason: The pass criterion is conditional on a drive around manoeuvre in the new scenario; o741 requires avoiding collision with the targets in a different scenario.

coverage.source_unit: Pedestrian target travels straight, perpendicular to VUT direction, constant 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from max 1 m of front of static target
Pedestrian target positioning coordinated so impact point is on VUT longitudinal centreline if VUT remains at speed when reaching rear of static target and does not brake

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test, the pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the VUT's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the front of the static target.
obligations.reason: The start position relative to the static target is new, and the old o705 'starting not before functional part' wording is absent. o705 is for a different scenario and not a continuation.

obligations.text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test, the pedestrian target's positioning shall be coordinated with the VUT so that the impact point of the pedestrian target on the front of the VUT is on the longitudinal centreline of the VUT if the VUT would remain at the speed it has when reaching the rear of the static target and does not brake.
obligations.reason: The reference point is the rear of the static target and no 0.2 m tolerance is stated, unlike o705; this is a separately scoped coordination requirement.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.18.2 Extended testing: demonstrate system not unreasonably changing control strategy for crossing pedestrian target

obligations.text: Extended testing for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre: the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing pedestrian target.
obligations.reason: Wording matches o706, but that clause belongs to the separate plain crossing-pedestrian scenario 4.2.5.2.9. This is a separately scoped test for the new drive around scenario, not a relocation.

coverage.source_unit: Test executed at least with (a) static and pedestrian target of different type and/or size
(b) pedestrian target moving at different but constant speed
(c) different angle of pedestrian target path to VUT path

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian crossing during drive around manoeuvre, the test shall be executed at least with a static and pedestrian target of a different type and/or size.
obligations.reason: Variation (a) differs from o707 (pedestrian size only) and applies to the new scenario's static target, so it is not an equivalent obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian crossing during drive around manoeuvre, the test shall be executed at least with a pedestrian target moving at a different, but constant speed.
obligations.reason: Same variation as o707(b), but applies to the separately introduced drive around scenario, so it is a new scoped obligation.

obligations.text: In the extended test for the pedestrian crossing during drive around manoeuvre, the test shall be executed at least with a different angle of the pedestrian target path to the VUT path.
obligations.reason: Same variation as o707(c), but applies to the separately introduced drive around scenario, so it is a new scoped obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19 heading: VUT crosses straight path of vehicle target in partially obstructed intersection
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only, with no independent obligation; the scenario title introduces the sub-paragraphs that carry the requirements.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.1 Base Test: test shall confirm declared response capability to recognize and offer right of way for crossing vehicle target driving straight in intersection (partially obstructed context)

obligations.text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the Base Test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system to recognize and offer right of way for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
obligations.reason: Wording matches o733 (4.2.5.2.14.1), but o733 is scoped to the unobstructed intersection scenario. This paragraph sits under a separately introduced partially obstructed intersection scenario (4.2.5.2.19), so it is a separately applicable test obligation, not a renumbering of o733.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.1.1 VUT approach to impact point with vehicle target from near side only, 25% along target length with VUT centre front

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection, the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line in an intersection from the near side direction, to collide the side of the target vehicle at 25 per cent along the length of the target with the centre front of the VUT.
obligations.reason: Candidate o734 allows either near side or far side direction in the unobstructed scenario. Here only the near side direction is specified and the scenario is the partially obstructed intersection, so it is a different scoped test setup and not the same obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.1.2 target approaches at speed up to 60 km/h depending on declared system boundaries
4.2.5.2.19.1.2 VUT is expected to give right of way

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection, the target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
obligations.reason: Similar to o729 (4.2.5.2.14.1.2), but that clause is scoped to the unobstructed intersection test. This is a separately applicable test parameter for the partially obstructed scenario.

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection, the VUT is expected to give right of way to the crossing target.
obligations.reason: Similar to the right-of-way expectation in o734 (4.2.5.2.14.1.2), but that applies to the unobstructed scenario. This is a separate expected-outcome criterion for the partially obstructed scenario.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.1.3 static target placed in opposite direction of travel on same side of intersection, obstructing view of the coming moving target without interfering with VUT path

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection, a static target shall be placed in the opposite direction of travel at the same side of the intersection, such that it obstructs the view of the coming moving target but does not interfere with the path of the VUT.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause sets up a static view-obstructing target; the candidates concern straight-line travel setups. This is a new test setup requirement.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.2 Extended testing: demonstrate system is not unreasonably changing control strategy for crossing vehicle target driving straight in intersection

obligations.text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario, the Extended test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
obligations.reason: Wording matches o735 (4.2.5.2.14.2), but o735 is under the unobstructed intersection scenario. This is a separately scoped extended test under the partially obstructed scenario 4.2.5.2.19, so it is not a relocation of o735.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.19.2.1 (a)-(d) test executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories, overlaps, lane positions of VUT and moving target, and positions of the static target

obligations.text: In the partially obstructed intersection extended testing, the test shall be executed at least with: (a) different target vehicle types or categories; (b) different overlaps; (c) different lane positions of the VUT and moving target vehicle; (d) different positions of the static target.
obligations.reason: Similar to o736 (4.2.5.2.14.2.1), but that is scoped to the unobstructed scenario and lacks item (d), the different positions of the static target. This is a separately scoped variation list for the partially obstructed scenario, not a renumbering.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20 heading: VUT turns across a path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist
4.2.5.2.20.1 Base Test: confirm declared response capability for oncoming vehicle target while VUT turns in intersection with multiple targets

obligations.text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist, the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection with multiple targets.
obligations.reason: Candidate o727 covers a single oncoming vehicle target without a cyclist. The new clause adds a multiple-target scenario, so it is a separately scoped test and not the same obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20.1.1 VUT approach in straight line then turn, 50 per cent overlap

obligations.text: In the Base Test with multiple targets (oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line followed by a turn in an intersection to cross the front edges of the target vehicle, with a lateral position giving a 50 per cent overlap of the width of the VUT.
obligations.reason: The wording matches o728, but it sits under the separately introduced multiple-target oncoming vehicle and cyclist test (4.2.5.2.20.1). This is a new scoped procedure, and there is no evidence of relocation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20.1.2 first target approach speed up to 60 km/h

obligations.text: In the Base Test with multiple targets (oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the first target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h.
obligations.reason: Candidate o729 concerns a crossing vehicle target in a different scenario and is conditioned on declared system boundaries. This one applies to the first target in the multi-target test, so it is a new scoped obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20.1.3 cyclist target speed 20 km/h +0/-0.4 and position within 1 m of road edge
4.2.5.2.20.1.3 cyclist positioning coordinated with target, reaching centreline two s after rear of moving target passes

obligations.text: In the Base Test with multiple targets (oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the cyclist target shall approach at 20 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the road edge.
obligations.reason: No old clause has a cyclist target in a turning-across-oncoming-vehicle test with these speed and position values. The candidates concern pedestrian targets or a different scenario.

obligations.text: In the Base Test with multiple targets (oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the cyclist target's positioning shall be coordinated with the moving target so that the cyclist target reaches the centreline of the road two s after the rear of the moving target passes the same virtual centreline.
obligations.reason: The timing coordination between the cyclist and the moving vehicle target is not present in any candidate old clause, so this is a new scoped test-procedure obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20.2 Extended testing: demonstrate system not unreasonably changing control strategy for oncoming vehicle target while VUT turns in intersection

obligations.text: In the Extended testing for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist, the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection.
obligations.reason: Candidate o730 has identical wording but belongs to the separate scenario 4.2.5.2.13 (no cyclist). The new clause is under the oncoming vehicle and cyclist scenario 4.2.5.2.20, so it is a separately applicable test and there is no positive evidence of relocation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2.5.2.20.2.1 intro + (a): extended test for VUT turning across oncoming vehicle/cyclist executed with different target vehicle types or categories
(b) Different overlaps
(c) Different lane position of the vehicles and target

obligations.text: For the extended test in 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist; demonstrating no unreasonable change of control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
obligations.reason: New scenario (VUT turns across path of oncoming vehicle and cyclist, 4.2.5.2.20). Similar wording in o736 and o731 applies to different scenarios (crossing path, oncoming vehicle turn), so it is a separate scoped obligation.

obligations.text: For the extended test in 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
obligations.reason: Separate scenario-scoped test case for the oncoming vehicle and cyclist turn; the old candidates belong to different scenarios.

obligations.text: For the extended test in 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the vehicles and target.
obligations.reason: Separate scenario-scoped test variation for the oncoming vehicle and cyclist turn; old candidates are for other scenarios.

obligations.text: The location and selection of the test route, time-of-day and environmental conditions for public road verification shall be determined by the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Identical scoped obligation as o745 (Annex 4 / 4.3.1), same paragraph number, same parent 4.3 Public Road Verification; only relocated page.

obligations.reason: Same requirement as in o745 (4.3.1) with unchanged scope.

obligations.text: Public road verification shall include scenarios in which the system is expected to experience challenging scenarios (e.g. tight curvatures, speed changes caused by variable infrastructural and traffic conditions, variable lead vehicle behaviour, variable road speed limits) and to approach the limits of its declared system boundaries (e.g. changes in visibility or road conditions, planned or sudden end of system boundaries).
obligations.reason: Same requirement as in o745 (4.3.1) with unchanged scope and examples.

coverage.source_unit: 4.3.2 duration of public road tests to allow recording and assessment per paragraphs 5 and 6, excluding safety critical and failure related scenarios

obligations.text: The duration of public road tests shall be such that it allows the recording and assessment of the system operation according to all relevant parts of the specification described in paragraphs 5. and 6., excluding safety critical and failure related scenarios.
obligations.reason: Identical to o746 (Annex 4 / 4.3.2), same paragraph and parent; unchanged.

obligations.reason: Same as o748 (Annex 4 / 4.3.3.1), same paragraph and parent; unchanged.

obligations.text: The routing shall be planned such that it incorporates the test scenarios which are relevant according to the declaration of the manufacturer in Annex 3 of this UN regulation.
obligations.reason: Same as o748 (4.3.3.1), unchanged.

obligations.text: The test plan created by the Type Approval Authority shall cover the scenarios to assess the specific capability in a variety of circumstances.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Illustrative non-exhaustive list of scenario types and references; scope of the evidence obligation, not a separate obligation

obligations.text: For public road verification of other driver- or system-initiated manoeuvres, the manufacturer shall additionally provide evidence of the system's behaviour in any type of scenario that is relevant according to the manufacturer's declaration in Annex 3 (e.g., based on virtual testing); scenario types include selecting a lane, roundabout entry/exit, leaving the lane of travel other than a lane change, taking a turn, and departing/arriving at a parked position (reference paras. 6.3.1–6.3.9.4, non-exhaustive).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o749 (Annex 4 / 4.3.3.2), identical wording and tables, renumbered pages only; same actor, action and scope.

obligations.reason: Identical to o750 (Annex 4 / 4.3.4) with same actor, scenario scope and TAA satisfaction condition.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority may log, or request logs of, any data channels used or generated by the system as deemed necessary for post-test evaluation of the public road verification drive.

obligations.text: It is recommended that management activities be established to support the M&S (whose lifecycle has frequent releases that should be monitored and documented) through typical product management processes, and that relevant information on the aspects listed in this section be included.

obligations.text: The notifying authority notifies the other authorities by adding a notification message onto DETA.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 4: information uploaded to DETA is only available to Contracting Parties applying UN Regulation No. (access restriction)

obligations.text: Information uploaded to DETA shall be made available only to the Contracting Parties applying UN Regulation No. 171.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph Annex 6/4 unchanged from o845; identical actor, object and scope.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 171: notification message in standardised text (para 6(c)) available to all DETA users

obligations.text: The notification message, in the form of the standardised text (see paragraph 6(c) of Annex 6), shall be available to all DETA users.
obligations.reason: Identical to o846 in same Annex 6 paragraph; no change in scope.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 5 first sentence: information obtained through DETA shall be protected in a secure manner
Annex 6 / 5 second sentence: information shall not be used for purposes other than preventing negative consequences of DCAS operation
Heading II. General guidance on the use of DETA

obligations.text: Information obtained through DETA for the purpose of the information sharing scheme defined in UN Regulation No. 171 shall be protected in a secure manner.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph as o847, unchanged wording and scope.

obligations.text: Information obtained through DETA for the information sharing scheme shall not be used for purposes other than preventing negative consequences of DCAS operation.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph as o847, unchanged restriction on use.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 6(a): notifying authority communicates with manufacturer
Annex 6 / 6(b): compile info of para 7.2.2.2 into pdf files and upload as type OTHER
Annex 6 / 6(c): enter notification in News tab with standard text and approval number
Note 1: News notification 2-month default expiry
Note 2: News is not a mailing system; recommendation to check daily
coverage.exclusion_reason: Informative guidance/recommendation, not a mandatory obligation

obligations.text: The notifying authority shall communicate with the manufacturer to understand fully the nature of the incident, the role of DCAS in it, its cause, and the remedial actions (to be) taken by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 6(a) as in o848, unchanged.

obligations.text: The notifying authority shall put all information required by UN Regulation No. 171 paragraph 7.2.2.2 together as one or more pdf files and upload them to the type-approval number concerned as document parts of type "OTHER".
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 6(b) as in o848, unchanged.

obligations.text: The notifying authority shall enter the notification in the DETA tab "News", including as a minimum the standard text (The Approval Authority of [country name] hereby notifies ... Please refer to the type-approval No. […] for the details) and the approval number to trace related information in the DETA archive.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 6(c) as in o848, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 7 first sentence: complete 6(b) and (c) ASAP, within 14 days of receiving remedial action info
Annex 6 / 7 second sentence: actions do not absolve authority from reporting non-conformities under Article 4 and Schedule 6 of 1958 Agreement

obligations.text: The notifying authority shall complete the actions of paragraph 6(b) and (c) as soon as possible but at least within 14 days of receiving the information on the remedial action from the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Identical to o849 in the same paragraph.

obligations.text: The actions under paragraph 6(b) and (c) do not absolve the notifying authority from the requirement to report non-conformities to other Contracting Parties, as outlined in Article 4 and Schedule 6 of the 1958 Agreement.
obligations.reason: Identical to o849 second sentence, unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: Annex 6 / 8: other approval authorities may submit queries via e-mail

obligations.text: Other approval authorities of Contracting Parties applying UN Regulation No. 171, having taken note of the notification message, may submit queries regarding the incident to the notifying authority via e-mail.
obligations.reason: Same permission as o850; only trailing quotation mark differs.
